children.title: Cubic-Regularized Model Interface
children.top_down_role: Boundary between restricted quadratic models and adaptive cubic regularization.

knowledge_statements.title: Cubic-Regularized Model Interface
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Unconstrained adaptive cubic regularization with a Euclidean cubic term.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
At \(x_k\in\mathbb R^n\), a cubic-regularized model interface supplies \(f_k\in\mathbb R\), \(g_k\in\mathbb R^n\), a symmetric \(B_k\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}\), and \(\sigma_k>0\), and defines
\[
m_k(s)=f_k+g_k^{\mathsf T}s+\tfrac12s^{\mathsf T}B_ks+\tfrac{\sigma_k}{3}\|s\|_2^3.
\]
Unlike a quadratic trust-region subproblem, the step need not satisfy an explicit radius constraint: coercivity of the positive cubic term ensures that \(m_k\) has a global minimizer. An exact global minimizer \(s_k\) satisfies \((B_k+\sigma_k\|s_k\|_2I)s_k=-g_k\) and \(B_k+\sigma_k\|s_k\|_2I\succeq0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A cubic interface augments a quadratic local model by a positive cubic norm term, yielding a coercive unconstrained step model and explicit stationarity conditions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(m_k\) is coercive and possesses a global minimizer satisfying the displayed first- and second-order conditions.

notation.meaning: global minimizer of the cubic model

review_flags: Supplied cubic-interpolation locators do not establish the adaptive cubic-regularization interface.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The cubic representation and its mathematical role fit the leaf. The coercivity and exact global-minimizer characterization are nontrivial claims and have no supporting locator; the supplied cubic-interpolation sources concern a different construction.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Cubic regularization of a quadratic local model
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: \(g_k\in\mathbb R^n\), \(B_k=B_k^T\), and \(\sigma_k>0\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Unconstrained smooth optimization using an isotropically cubic-regularized quadratic model, without a separate hard trust-region constraint.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A cubic-regularized model interface is \[m_k^{C}(p)=f(x_k)+g_k^Tp+	frac12p^TB_kp+	frac{\sigma_k}{3}\|p\|_2^3,
\qquad p\in\mathbb R^n,\] where \(g_k\) and \(B_k\) represent first- and second-order local information and \(\sigma_k>0\) is the regularization parameter. The cubic term makes the model coercive even when \(B_k\) is indefinite. The interface exposes the same linear and curvature data as a quadratic trust-region model together with \(\sigma_k\), but controls step size through the cubic penalty rather than the constraint \(\|p\|\leq\Delta_k\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A cubic-regularized model adds \(\sigma_k\|p\|_2^3/3\) to a quadratic local model. The positive regularization parameter makes the model grow without bound as the step norm grows, even if the quadratic curvature is indefinite. It therefore controls the step through a penalty rather than through a hard trust-region radius.
assumptions_latex: The Euclidean norm is used in the cubic term.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The displayed coercive function is the cubic-regularized local-model interface.
equivalent_formulations_latex: For \(p\neq0\), stationarity is \(g_k+B_kp+\sigma_k\|p\|_2p=0\).
special_cases_latex: With exact data, \(g_k=\nabla f(x_k)\) and \(B_k=\nabla^2f(x_k)\).
immediate_consequences_latex: Because \(\sigma_k>0\), \(m_k^C(p)\to+\infty\) as \(\|p\|_2\to\infty\), so a global minimizer exists.
boundary_notes: This is not a quadratic trust-region subproblem unless a separate radius constraint is imposed.
No precise supporting locator for this definition was present in the supplied source hints.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: One-Step Decrease for the Modified Accelerated Cubic Newton Method
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conditional decrease estimate for the modified method; the extract invokes additional hypotheses of an earlier theorem that are not expanded here.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\) be convex with \(x^*\in\arg\min f\). Assume all hypotheses required for the method \(\mathcal M'\), including constants \(\sigma_2,L_3>0\) and, for every \(k\ge0\), points \(\hat x_k,x_{k+1}\) satisfying
\[
f(x_k)\ge f(\hat x_k)\ge f(x_{k+1}),
\]
\[
f(\hat x_k)-f(x_{k+1})\ge\frac{\sigma_2}{6}\|x_{k+1}-\hat x_k\|^3,
\]
and
\[
\|x_{k+1}-\hat x_k\|\ge\frac{\sqrt{2\sigma_2}}{L_3}[f(x_{k+1})-f(x^*)]^{1/6}.
\]
If \(M=2L_3\), then for every \(k\ge0\),
\[
f(x_k)-f(x_{k+1})\ge f(\hat x_k)-f(x_{k+1})\ge\frac{\sqrt2\,\sigma_2^{3/2}}{3L_3}[f(x_{k+1})-f(x^*)]^{1/2}.
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a convex objective, if every modified accelerated cubic Newton step is monotone, satisfies the stated cubic decrease inequality, and has the stated suboptimality-controlled length, then choosing M equal to twice L3 gives the displayed square-root suboptimality lower bound on every one-step objective decrease.
assumptions_latex: \text{All other hypotheses invoked for }\mathcal M'\text{ hold}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \forall k\ge0:\quad f(x_k)-f(x_{k+1})\ge f(\hat x_k)-f(x_{k+1})\ge\frac{\sqrt2\,\sigma_2^{3/2}}{3L_3}[f(x_{k+1})-f(x^*)]^{1/2}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Scale-indexed model accuracy class
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: \(f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\), model class \(\mathcal M\), centers \(x\in S\), and radii \(0<\Delta\leq\Delta_{\max}\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Uniform deterministic accuracy classes indexed by the trust-region scale and derivative order.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(q\in\{1,2\}\), a model class \(\mathcal M\) is a deterministic order-\(q\) accuracy class for \(f\) if constants \(\kappa_0,\ldots,\kappa_q>0\), independent of \(x\) and \(\Delta\), exist such that for every admissible \((x,\Delta)\) one can select \(m\in\mathcal M\) satisfying \[\|D^jf(y)-D^jm(y)\|\leq\kappa_j\Delta^{q+1-j},
\qquad j=0,\ldots,q,
\quad y\in B(x;\Delta).\] For \(j=0\), the norm denotes absolute value. The class must also admit a uniformly finite procedure that certifies such a model or replaces it by one satisfying these bounds.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An order-\(q\) model accuracy class provides, at every admissible center and radius, a model whose errors in derivatives of orders zero through \(q\) scale respectively as \(\Delta^{q+1-j}\). The constants are uniform, and a finite uniformly bounded procedure must be able to certify or construct an accurate member. Orders one and two correspond to fully linear and fully quadratic classes.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) and candidate models possess the derivatives appearing through order \(q\).
The corresponding highest derivative has the regularity needed for uniform Taylor-type bounds.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The derivative-error inequalities and finite certification requirement define the deterministic model accuracy class of order \(q\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: For \(q=1\), the errors are \(O(\Delta^2)\) in value and \(O(\Delta)\) in gradient.
For \(q=2\), the errors are \(O(\Delta^3)\), \(O(\Delta^2)\), and \(O(\Delta)\) in value, gradient, and Hessian.
special_cases_latex: Fully linear and fully quadratic model classes are the \(q=1\) and \(q=2\) instances.
immediate_consequences_latex: The definition compares accuracy at a common trust-region scale and permits different model constructions at different centers and radii.
boundary_notes: The definition is deterministic; probability-qualified models require separate quantifiers.
A class may contain inaccurate members, provided an accurate member can be selected or produced.

notation.meaning: Derivative of order j, with order zero interpreted as the function value.

source_refs.locator: Section 6.1, Definitions 6.1 and 6.2, equations (6.1)–(6.5), pp. 90–92

review_flags: The compact order-q notation consolidates the two explicitly sourced definitions without extending beyond q equal to one or two.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Uniform deterministic trust-region accuracy
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: \(f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\), \(x\in S\), \(0<\Delta\leq\Delta_{\max}\), and \(m\) is defined on a neighborhood of \(B(x;\Delta)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Nonrandom, uniform first- or second-order fidelity on every point of a trust-region ball.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Deterministic model accuracy requires the prescribed value and derivative error bounds to hold at every point of the trust-region ball, without probability or exceptional outcomes. At order one, the value and gradient errors scale as \(\Delta^2\) and \(\Delta\). At order two, value, gradient, and Hessian errors scale as \(\Delta^3\), \(\Delta^2\), and \(\Delta\). Uniform accuracy uses constants independent of the center and radius.
assumptions_latex: The derivatives through order \(q\) exist on the relevant ball.
The constants \(\kappa_j\) are finite and independent of \(y\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The universal error bounds define deterministic order-\(q\) accuracy on \(B(x;\Delta)\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: The quantifier is \(\forall y\in B(x;\Delta)\), rather than an expectation or high-probability statement.
special_cases_latex: Order one is fully linear pointwise accuracy.
Order two is fully quadratic pointwise accuracy.
immediate_consequences_latex: At the center, \(\|D^jf(x)-D^jm(x)\|\leq\kappa_j\Delta^{q+1-j}\) for every represented derivative order.
boundary_notes: This definition does not cover biased estimators, random models, or accuracy only in expectation.
A single accurate model is distinct from an accuracy class with a model-improvement procedure.

notation.meaning: Deterministic fidelity order, one or two.

knowledge_statements.title: Fully Linear Models
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Deterministic first-order fidelity on a closed trust-region ball.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\) be continuously differentiable, let \(x\in\mathbb R^n\), and let \(\Delta>0\). A continuously differentiable model \(m\) is fully linear for \(f\) on \(B(x,\Delta)=\{y:\|y-x\|\leq\Delta\}\) with constants \(\kappa_{ef},\kappa_{eg}\geq0\) if, for every \(y\in B(x,\Delta)\),
\[
|f(y)-m(y)|\leq\kappa_{ef}\Delta^2,
\qquad
\|\nabla f(y)-\nabla m(y)\|\leq\kappa_{eg}\Delta.
\]
For a model family, the constants are required to be independent of the center and radius over the algorithmically admitted collection of balls.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A fully linear model approximates function values to order radius squared and gradients to order radius throughout the trust region.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) and \(m\) are continuously differentiable on a neighborhood of \(B(x,\Delta)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(m\) has uniform first-order fidelity to \(f\) on \(B(x,\Delta)\).

notation.meaning: closed norm ball centered at x with radius Delta
uniform function and gradient error constants

knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: \(f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\) has Lipschitz-continuous gradient on an open neighborhood of \(\bigcup_{x\in S}B(x;\Delta_{\max})\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Deterministic derivative-free or model-based first-order trust-region accuracy in Euclidean space.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A class \(\mathcal M\subset C^1(\mathbb R^n)\) is fully linear for \(f\) on \(S\) up to radius \(\Delta_{\max}\) if constants \(\kappa_{ef},\kappa_{eg},
u_1^m>0\) exist such that, for every \(x\in S\) and \(0<\Delta\leq\Delta_{\max}\), there is \(m\in\mathcal M\) whose gradient is Lipschitz with constant at most \(
u_1^m\) and \[|f(y)-m(y)|\leq\kappa_{ef}\Delta^2,
\qquad \|
abla f(y)-
abla m(y)\|\leq\kappa_{eg}\Delta
\quad orall y\in B(x;\Delta).\] In addition, a uniformly finite model-improvement procedure must either certify a given model as fully linear on the ball or produce one that is.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A fully linear class provides, for every admissible center and radius, a continuously differentiable model with uniformly Lipschitz gradient whose function error is at most \(\kappa_{ef}\Delta^2\) and whose gradient error is at most \(\kappa_{eg}\Delta\) throughout the ball. A uniformly bounded finite procedure must be able to certify such accuracy or construct an accurate replacement.
assumptions_latex: \(f\in C^1\) on the relevant open domain.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The class \(\mathcal M\) is fully linear precisely when it satisfies the uniform value, gradient, regularity, and model-improvement requirements.
equivalent_formulations_latex: A particular member satisfying the two bounds is fully linear on \(B(x;\Delta)\).
special_cases_latex: A suitably accurate first-order Taylor or interpolation model can be fully linear.
Linear polynomial models on uniformly well-poised sample sets form fully linear classes.
immediate_consequences_latex: At the center, the model value and gradient converge to those of \(f\) at rates \(O(\Delta^2)\) and \(O(\Delta)\).
boundary_notes: The definition concerns a class and a certification mechanism, not merely one model.
It does not require every class member to satisfy the bounds for every ball.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Hölder Hessian Upper Model
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Bounds the second-order Taylor remainder under Hölder continuity of the Hessian; convexity of the function is not assumed.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(Q\) be convex in a finite-dimensional normed space, and use the induced operator norm for linear maps. Let \(f:Q	o\mathbb R\) be twice differentiable. If, for some \(v\in(0,1]\) and \(H_v\in[0,+\infty]\), \(\|
abla^2f(x)-
abla^2f(y)\|\le H_v\|x-y\|^v\) for all \(x,y\in Q\), then for all \(x,y\in Q\), \[f(y)\le f(x)+\langle
abla f(x),y-xangle+ rac12\langle
abla^2f(x)(y-x),y-xangle+ rac{H_v\|y-x\|^{2+v}}{(1+v)(2+v)}.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a twice-differentiable function on a convex set, a Hölder-continuous Hessian bounds the function above by its quadratic Taylor model plus an explicit remainder of order 2+v. The statement does not require the function to be convex.
assumptions_latex: \((\mathbb E,\|\cdot\|)\) is finite-dimensional, and the same notation denotes the induced operator norm.
\(Q\subset\mathbb E\) is convex and \(f:Q\to\mathbb R\) is twice differentiable.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\forall x,y\in Q:\ f(y)\le f(x)+\langle\nabla f(x),y-x\rangle+\frac12\langle\nabla^2f(x)(y-x),y-x\rangle+\frac{H_v\|y-x\|^{2+v}}{(1+v)(2+v)}.\)

knowledge_statements.title: Fully Quadratic Models
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Deterministic second-order fidelity on a closed trust-region ball.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\) be twice continuously differentiable, let \(x\in\mathbb R^n\), and let \(\Delta>0\). A twice continuously differentiable model \(m\) is fully quadratic for \(f\) on \(B(x,\Delta)\) with constants \(\kappa_{ef},\kappa_{eg},\kappa_{eh}\geq0\) if every \(y\in B(x,\Delta)\) satisfies
\[
|f(y)-m(y)|\leq\kappa_{ef}\Delta^3,
\quad \|\nabla f(y)-\nabla m(y)\|\leq\kappa_{eg}\Delta^2,
\quad \|\nabla^2f(y)-\nabla^2m(y)\|\leq\kappa_{eh}\Delta.
\]
For a model family, these constants are uniform over the admitted centers and radii.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A fully quadratic model approximates values, gradients, and Hessians to orders three, two, and one in the trust-region radius.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) and \(m\) are twice continuously differentiable on a neighborhood of \(B(x,\Delta)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(m\) has uniform second-order fidelity to \(f\) on \(B(x,\Delta)\).

notation.meaning: closed norm ball centered at x with radius Delta
uniform value, gradient, and Hessian error constants

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Imperfect local-model accuracy class
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\), let \(x_k\in\mathbb R^n\) and \(\Delta_k>0\), and let the iteration-dependent model \(m_k:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\) be defined on \(B_k=\{x:\|x-x_k\|\leq\Delta_k\}\). Let \(\mathcal F_{k-1}\) denote the information available before constructing \(m_k\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional local models whose fidelity can be approximate, conditional, or random; no convergence assertion is included.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: An imperfect model-accuracy specification is a sequence of events \(A_k(\delta)\), for \(0<\delta\leq\Delta_k\), and constants \(\kappa_f,\kappa_g\geq0\) such that on \(A_k(\delta)\), \[|f(x)-m_k(x)|\leq\kappa_f\delta^2\quad(\|x-x_k\|\leq\delta),\qquad \|\nabla f(x_k)-\nabla m_k(x_k)\|\leq\kappa_g\delta.\] The specification is deterministic if \(A_k(\delta)\) always holds, conditional if an algorithmically testable predicate implies \(A_k(\delta)\), and probabilistic at level \(p\in(0,1]\) if \(\mathbb P(A_k(\delta)\mid\mathcal F_{k-1})\geq p\) almost surely. A model family is imperfectly accurate when it is assigned at least one of these non-unconditional qualifications.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For an objective \(f\), center \(x_k\), radius \(\Delta_k\), and local model \(m_k\), an imperfect accuracy class is specified by events \(A_k(\delta)\). Whenever the event occurs, the function-value error throughout the radius-\(\delta\) ball is at most \(\kappa_f\delta^2\), and the gradient error at the center is at most \(\kappa_g\delta\). The qualification may be deterministic, triggered by a checkable condition, or probabilistic through a conditional-probability lower bound given past information. Thus the term denotes a fidelity requirement that need not hold unconditionally at every iteration.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(m_k\) belongs to the specified imperfect accuracy class exactly when the stated error bounds hold on the associated event \(A_k(\delta)\), with the declared deterministic, conditional, or probabilistic quantifier.
equivalent_formulations_latex: Writing \(e_k(x)=f(x)-m_k(x)\), the value condition is \(\sup_{\|x-x_k\|\leq\delta}|e_k(x)|/\delta^2\leq\kappa_f\) on \(A_k(\delta)\).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Trust-region iteration with magical steps
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Specifies the complete acceptance and radius-update rules; the referenced sufficient-decrease and magical-step conditions remain named because their formulas are absent from the extract.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Given \(x_0\), \(\Delta_0\), and constants \(\eta_1,\eta_2,\gamma_1,\gamma_2\) satisfying (6.1.3), at iteration \(k\) choose \(\|\cdot\|_k\) and a model \(m_k\) on \(\mathcal B_k\). Compute \(s_k\) satisfying AA.1 and \(x_k+s_k\in\mathcal B_k\), and compute \(s_k^{\mathrm{MA}}\) satisfying (10.4.1). Define
\[
\rho_k^{\mathrm{MA}}=\frac{f(x_k)-f(x_k+s_k+s_k^{\mathrm{MA}})}{m_k(x_k)-m_k(x_k+s_k)+f(x_k+s_k)-f(x_k+s_k+s_k^{\mathrm{MA}})}.
\]
Set \(x_{k+1}=x_k+s_k+s_k^{\mathrm{MA}}\) if \(\rho_k^{\mathrm{MA}}\geq\eta_1\), and \(x_{k+1}=x_k\) otherwise. Choose
\[
\Delta_{k+1}\in
\begin{cases}
[\Delta_k,\infty),&\rho_k^{\mathrm{MA}}\geq\eta_2,\\
[\gamma_2\Delta_k,\Delta_k],&\eta_1\leq\rho_k^{\mathrm{MA}}<\eta_2,\\
[\gamma_1\Delta_k,\gamma_2\Delta_k],&\rho_k^{\mathrm{MA}}<\eta_1,
\end{cases}
\]
and repeat.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At each iteration, compute a sufficiently model-reducing trust-region step and an auxiliary magical step. Accept their sum when the adjusted actual-to-predicted reduction ratio is at least eta_1; otherwise retain the current point. Enlarge or retain the radius when the ratio is at least eta_2, choose a nonincreasing radius in the intermediate regime, and contract it within the stated gamma-scaled interval after an unsuccessful iteration.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: x_{k+1}=\begin{cases}x_k+s_k+s_k^{\mathrm{MA}},&\rho_k^{\mathrm{MA}}\geq\eta_1,\\x_k,&\rho_k^{\mathrm{MA}}<\eta_1,\end{cases}\quad \Delta_{k+1}\in\begin{cases}[\Delta_k,\infty),&\rho_k^{\mathrm{MA}}\geq\eta_2,\\[\gamma_2\Delta_k,\Delta_k],&\eta_1\leq\rho_k^{\mathrm{MA}}<\eta_2,\\[\gamma_1\Delta_k,\gamma_2\Delta_k],&\rho_k^{\mathrm{MA}}<\eta_1.\end{cases}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Full gradient convergence under a bounded magical step
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Strengthens subsequential criticality to full-sequence convergence by uniformly bounding each magical step relative to the trust-region radius.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Suppose AF.1--AF.2, AN.1, (10.4.5), AM.1--AM.4, and (10.4.6) hold, and let \(\{x_k\}\) be generated by the magical-step trust-region algorithm. If there exists \(\kappa_{\mathrm{mms}}>0\) such that, for every \(k\),

knowledge_statements.title: Conditional Models
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Pathwise fidelity imposed only when an algorithmic trigger is active.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(m_k\) be a model on \(B(x_k,\Delta_k)\), let \(T_k\in\{0,1\}\) be an algorithmically specified trigger measurable from information available when the model is assessed, and let \(\mathcal A_k\) denote a chosen deterministic fidelity predicate, such as full linearity. The sequence is conditionally accurate relative to \((T_k)\) when
\[
T_k=1\;\Longrightarrow\;\mathcal A_k(m_k;f,x_k,\Delta_k)\text{ holds}
\]
for every iteration \(k\). No accuracy assertion is imposed when \(T_k=0\). The trigger must be fixed independently of whether the unobserved fidelity inequalities happen to hold, so the implication cannot be made vacuous by inspecting their failure.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A conditional model must meet a specified fidelity predicate whenever a predeclared algorithmic trigger is active; inactive iterations carry no fidelity requirement.
assumptions_latex: \(T_k\) is determined by information available at model assessment.
\(\mathcal A_k\) is a precisely specified deterministic fidelity predicate.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(T_k=1\) guarantees the required model-accuracy event \(\mathcal A_k\).
review_flags: Conditional-model terminology is not uniquely standardized without a designated algorithmic framework.
A source is needed to confirm the intended trigger convention.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: A condition is an appropriate knowledge kind, but this trigger-based meaning of “conditional models” is framework-dependent. knowledge_statements.statement_title: Conditionally valid trust-region model
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\), let \(x_k\in\mathbb R^n\), and let \(m_k:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\) be twice differentiable. For \(\delta>0\), set \(Q_k(\delta)=\{x\in\mathbb R^n:\|x-x_k\|\leq\delta\}\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Deterministic finite-dimensional conditional models with a checkable validity condition and finitely terminating model improvement.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The model \(m_k\) is valid in \(Q_k(\delta)\) if there is a constant \(\kappa_{\mathrm{cnd}}>0\), independent of \(x\), such that \[|f(x)-m_k(x)|\leq\kappa_{\mathrm{cnd}}\delta^2\qquad\text{for every }x\in Q_k(\delta).\] It is a conditional model if this validity property is required only when a designated, algorithmically checkable condition \(C_k(\delta)\) holds, validity can be checked for every \(k\) and \(\delta>0\), and for every \(k,\delta\) a finite sequence of model-improvement operations can produce a model for which \(C_k(\delta)\) and hence the displayed bound hold.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A model \(m_k\) is valid on the ball \(Q_k(\delta)\) when its error from \(f\) is uniformly bounded there by \(\kappa_{\mathrm{cnd}}\delta^2\). It is conditional when this error guarantee is attached to a designated condition that can be tested by the algorithm, rather than imposed at every construction, and when any failed condition can be made true after finitely many model-improvement operations for every positive radius. The definition therefore includes both the fidelity inequality and the finite repair requirement.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(m_k\) is conditionally valid on \(Q_k(\delta)\) precisely when the checkable condition \(C_k(\delta)\) certifies the uniform \(O(\delta^2)\) value error and failed validity can be restored in finitely many improvement steps.
equivalent_formulations_latex: The validity inequality is \(\sup_{x\in Q_k(\delta)}|f(x)-m_k(x)|\leq\kappa_{\mathrm{cnd}}\delta^2\).
special_cases_latex: For interpolation models, \(C_k(\delta)\) may require an adequately poised interpolation set contained in \(Q_k(\delta)\).
An improvement operation may add a newly evaluated point in \(Q_k(\delta)\) and rebuild the model.
immediate_consequences_latex: Validity applies in particular at \(x_k\) and at every trial point lying in \(Q_k(\delta)\).
The finite-improvement condition excludes a model defect that persists forever at a fixed center and radius.
boundary_notes: Conditional validity is stronger than merely observing a good reduction ratio at one trial point because its error bound is uniform over the ball.
No probability qualification is part of this deterministic definition.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Modified Final Criticality Test for Second-Order Conditional Models
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Modified Step 1 of Algorithm 9.1.1; symbols retain the source algorithm's notation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At iteration k, if \lVert g_k\rVert\leq\epsilon_c, test whether m_k is second-order valid in \mathcal Q_k(\delta_k) for some \delta_k\leq\mu\max\!\left\{\lVert g_k\rVert,-\lambda_{\min}\!\left[\nabla_{xx}m_k(x_k)\right]\right\}. If so, go to Step 2. Otherwise, perform as many model-improvement steps as necessary to make m_k second-order valid in \[\mathcal Q_k\!\left(\alpha\mu\max\!\left\{\lVert g_k\rVert,-\lambda_{\min}\!\left[\nabla_{xx}m_k(x_k)\right]\right\}\right).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: When the gradient norm is at most the criticality tolerance, test second-order model validity on a neighborhood with an admissible radius bounded by the scaled maximum of the gradient norm and the model's negative minimum curvature. Proceed to Step 2 if the test succeeds; otherwise improve the model until it is second-order valid on the prescribed smaller neighborhood.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Conditional-model function-value error bound from poised local interpolation geometry
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sufficient interpolation-geometry conditions for uniform function-value accuracy of a conditional derivative-free trust-region model.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose AF.1, AF.3, and AF.5 hold, and let \(m_k\) have the form (9.4.9). Let \(Y\) be poised, let \(|Y|\ge n+1\), and suppose \(y\in\mathcal Q_k(\delta)\) for every \(y\in Y\). If the Newton fundamental polynomials satisfy \(\left|N_i^{[\ell]}\!\left(y_j^{[\ell+1]}\right)\right|\le\kappa_{\mathrm{nfp}}\) for every \(i=1,\ldots,|Y^{[\ell]}|\), \(j=1,\ldots,|Y^{[\ell+1]}|\), and \(\ell=0,\ldots,d-1\), and \(\left|N_i^{[d]}(x)\right|\le\kappa_{\mathrm{nfp}}\) for every \(i=1,\ldots,|Y^{[d]}|\) and \(x\in\mathcal Q_k(\delta)\), then there exists \(\kappa_{\mathrm{cnd}}>0\), independent of \(k\), such that \(\left|f(x)-m_k(x)\right|\le\kappa_{\mathrm{cnd}}\max\{\delta^2,\delta^3\}\) for every \(x\in\mathcal Q_k(\delta)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Assume AF.1, AF.3, and AF.5 and a model of form (9.4.9). If the interpolation set is poised, has at least the fully linear interpolation size of n+1 points, lies in the local region, and its specified Newton fundamental polynomials are uniformly bounded, then the function-value error throughout that region is bounded by a constant independent of the iteration times the maximum of delta squared and delta cubed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \exists\kappa_{\mathrm{cnd}}>0\text{ independent of }k\text{ such that }\left|f(x)-m_k(x)\right|\le\kappa_{\mathrm{cnd}}\max\{\delta^2,\delta^3\}\quad\forall x\in\mathcal Q_k(\delta).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Progress and model-improvement properties of the conditional trust-region algorithm
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Consequences of assumptions AM.7 and AM.8 for successful iterations, reference-radius resets, and a nonterminating criticality model-improvement loop.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose $\mathrm{AM}.7$ and $\mathrm{AM}.8$ hold. Then: (i) if $\rho_k\geq\eta_1$, then $\widehat\rho_k\geq\eta_0$, so iteration $k$ is successful; moreover, $\mathcal S\subseteq\mathcal R$. (ii) Only finitely many iterations satisfying $\rho_k<\eta_1$ can occur before $\Delta_{\mathrm{ref}}$ is set to $\Delta_k$. (iii) If the loop in Step 1 is infinite at iteration $k$, then $\nabla_x f(x_k)=0$ and $\lim_{i\to\infty}\lVert g_k^{(i)}\rVert=0$, where $g_k^{(i)}$ is the gradient at $x_k$ of the $i$th successive model computed in that loop.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under assumptions AM.7 and AM.8, strong trial-step agreement makes the iteration successful, every successful iteration belongs to the reference-radius-reset set, only finitely many inadequate-agreement iterations can precede the specified reset, and an infinite Step 1 model-improvement loop implies stationarity of the objective at the current point while the successive model gradients converge to zero.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \rho_k\geq\eta_1\Rightarrow\widehat\rho_k\geq\eta_0,\qquad \mathcal S\subseteq\mathcal R;\quad \text{only finitely many iterations with }\rho_k<\eta_1\text{ precede the stated reset};\quad \text{an infinite Step 1 loop implies }\nabla_x f(x_k)=0\text{ and }\lVert g_k^{(i)}\rVert\to0.

knowledge_statements.title: Models with Approximate Derivatives
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Radius-scaled derivative errors sufficient for quadratic-model fidelity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(f\) have an \(L_H\)-Lipschitz Hessian on \(B(x,\Delta)\), and define
\[
m(x+s)=f(x)+\widetilde g^{\mathsf T}s+\tfrac12s^{\mathsf T}\widetilde Hs.
\]
If \(\|\widetilde g-\nabla f(x)\|\leq\kappa_g\Delta^2\) and \(\|\widetilde H-\nabla^2f(x)\|\leq\kappa_H\Delta\), then, for every \(s\) satisfying \(\|s\|\leq\Delta\),
\[
|f(x+s)-m(x+s)|\leq\left(\kappa_g+\tfrac12\kappa_H+\tfrac16L_H\right)\Delta^3.
\]
The same derivative-error scaling, together with Hessian Lipschitz continuity, yields gradient error of order \(\Delta^2\) and Hessian error of order \(\Delta\), and hence fully quadratic fidelity with suitable uniform constants.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Gradient errors of order radius squared and Hessian errors of order radius make a centered quadratic model fully quadratic under Lipschitz-Hessian regularity.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) is twice continuously differentiable and \(\nabla^2 f\) is \(L_H\)-Lipschitz on \(B(x,\Delta)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The approximate-derivative quadratic model is fully quadratic on \(B(x,\Delta)\), with constants determined by \(\kappa_g\), \(\kappa_H\), and \(L_H\).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Trust-region model with controlled approximate derivatives
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\) be differentiable, let \(x_k\in\mathbb R^n\), and define \(m_k(x_k+s)=m_k(x_k)+g_k^Ts+\tfrac12s^TH_ks\), where \(H_k=H_k^T\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional smooth trust-region models with inexact gradients and finite-difference or quasi-Newton curvature approximations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A quadratic model has controlled approximate derivatives if its gradient error \(v_k=\nabla f(x_k)-g_k\) satisfies \[\|v_k\|\leq\kappa_{\mathrm{egg}}\|g_k\|\quad\text{for every }k\] for a fixed admissible \(\kappa_{\mathrm{egg}}\geq0\), and its symmetric curvature matrix \(H_k\) is generated by a declared approximation rule. Admissible rules include finite differences with a stated difference vector \(h_k\), or a secant update satisfying \[H_{k+1}s_k=y_k,\qquad y_k=g_{k+1}-g_k,\] whenever the update denominator required by the selected formula is nonzero. The model class records both the error control and the derivative-construction rule.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A quadratic trust-region model with approximate derivatives uses a model gradient \(g_k\) and symmetric curvature approximation \(H_k\) in place of exact derivatives. The gradient discrepancy \(v_k=\nabla f(x_k)-g_k\) must be bounded relative to the model gradient by a fixed constant. The curvature approximation must come from an explicitly declared mechanism, such as finite differences or a symmetric quasi-Newton update satisfying the secant equation. Thus merely labeling derivatives approximate is insufficient: the approximation error and update domain must be specified.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The model belongs to the controlled approximate-derivative class when \(\|\nabla f(x_k)-g_k\|\leq\kappa_{\mathrm{egg}}\|g_k\|\) and \(H_k\) is produced by its stated well-defined finite-difference or secant rule.
equivalent_formulations_latex: If \(\kappa_{\mathrm{egg}}<1\), then \((1-\kappa_{\mathrm{egg}})\|g_k\|\leq\|\nabla f(x_k)\|\leq(1+\kappa_{\mathrm{egg}})\|g_k\|\).
special_cases_latex: The BFGS rule is defined when \(y_k^Ts_k>0\).
The SR1 rule is defined when \((y_k-H_ks_k)^Ts_k\neq0\).
A forward finite-difference gradient uses \([g_k]_i=(f(x_k+[h_k]_ie_i)-f(x_k))/|[h_k]_i|\).
immediate_consequences_latex: If \(g_{k_j}\to0\) along a subsequence, the relative-error condition forces \(\nabla f(x_{k_j})\to0\).
boundary_notes: Finite-precision noise limits how far finite-difference steps can be reduced reliably.
First-order error control alone does not ensure that an approximate Hessian detects all negative curvature.

notation.meaning: Error of the model gradient relative to the objective gradient.
Difference of successive model gradients used in a secant equation.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Finite-difference, automatic, and symbolic derivative calculation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Describes three derivative-acquisition approaches without asserting an error order or convergence guarantee for the finite-difference formula.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For a smooth function $f:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}$, a small scalar $\epsilon>0$, and the $i$th unit vector $e_i$, the partial derivative at $x$ may be approximated by the central difference
\[
\frac{\partial f}{\partial x_i}(x)\approx\frac{f(x+\epsilon e_i)-f(x-\epsilon e_i)}{2\epsilon}.
\]
Automatic differentiation obtains derivatives by decomposing function-evaluation code into elementary operations and applying the chain rule, either by generating derivative-evaluation code or by recording and processing the executed operations at the evaluation point. Symbolic differentiation instead manipulates an algebraic specification of $f$ to produce expressions for the components of $\nabla f$.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a smooth real-valued function on Euclidean space, the ith partial derivative at a point can be approximated from function values at small positive and negative perturbations along the ith coordinate direction. Automatic differentiation applies the chain rule to the elementary operations in evaluation code, while symbolic differentiation manipulates an algebraic function specification to produce gradient-component expressions.
assumptions_latex: e_i\text{ is the }i\text{th standard unit vector}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \frac{\partial f}{\partial x_i}(x)\approx\frac{f(x+\epsilon e_i)-f(x-\epsilon e_i)}{2\epsilon}

knowledge_statements.title: Probabilistically Accurate Models
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conditional-probability formulation for random trust-region models.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(M_k\) be a random model, let \(\mathcal F_{k-1}\) contain the algorithmic history available before \(M_k\) is generated, and let \(\mathcal A_k\) be the event that \(M_k\) satisfies a specified deterministic fidelity predicate on \(B(X_k,\Delta_k)\). For \(p\in(0,1]\), the models are probabilistically \(p\)-accurate if
\[
\mathbb P(\mathcal A_k\mid\mathcal F_{k-1})\geq p
\quad\text{almost surely for every }k.
\]
The event may encode fully linear or fully quadratic inequalities with constants fixed independently of \(k\); the conditioning permits adaptive centers and radii while requiring a uniform lower probability of accuracy.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A random model is probabilistically accurate when, conditional on the past, its deterministic fidelity event has probability at least a fixed value.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathbb P(\mathcal A_k\mid\mathcal F_{k-1})\geq p\) almost surely at every iteration.
review_flags: No supplied locator covers probabilistic trust-region model accuracy.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: A definition is appropriate for this leaf, and the conditional-probability formulation is coherent. The filtration timing and accuracy-event convention vary across stochastic trust-region frameworks, so a specific source is required.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.statement_title: Probabilistically fully linear local model
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \((\Omega,\mathcal F,\mathbb P)\) be a probability space with filtration \((\mathcal F_k)\). Let \(X_k\), \(\Delta_k>0\), and the random model \(M_k\) be measurable with the model constructed after observing \(\mathcal F_{k-1}\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional stochastic local models with conditional, iterationwise fidelity events; independence across iterations is not assumed.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Fix \(p\in(0,1]\) and constants \(\kappa_f,\kappa_g\geq0\). Define \[A_k=\left\{\sup_{\|s\|\leq\Delta_k}|f(X_k+s)-M_k(X_k+s)|\leq\kappa_f\Delta_k^2,\quad \|\nabla f(X_k)-\nabla M_k(X_k)\|\leq\kappa_g\Delta_k\right\}.\] The random model sequence is probabilistically accurate at level \(p\) if \[\mathbb P(A_k\mid\mathcal F_{k-1})\geq p\quad\text{almost surely for every }k.\] The conditional bound, rather than an unconditional marginal probability, is part of the class definition.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A random local model is probabilistically accurate at level \(p\) when, conditionally on all information available before the current model is generated, it has probability at least \(p\) of satisfying both a uniform \(O(\Delta_k^2)\) function-value error over the trust region and an \(O(\Delta_k)\) gradient error at its center. This requirement is imposed at every iteration and does not require the model events to be independent.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \((M_k)\) belongs to the probabilistically accurate class exactly when \(\mathbb P(A_k\mid\mathcal F_{k-1})\geq p\) almost surely for all \(k\), with \(A_k\) equal to the displayed fidelity event.
equivalent_formulations_latex: The condition is \(\mathbb E[\mathbf 1_{A_k}\mid\mathcal F_{k-1}]\geq p\) almost surely.
special_cases_latex: For \(p=1\), the accuracy event holds conditionally almost surely.
If \(M_k\) is deterministic given \(\mathcal F_{k-1}\), the condition reduces to deterministic accuracy whenever \(p>0\).
immediate_consequences_latex: The definition permits temporally dependent model errors provided the iterationwise conditional success probability is maintained.
boundary_notes: An unconditional inequality \(\mathbb P(A_k)\geq p\) alone does not satisfy this definition.
The supplied sources do not establish the exact filtration convention or constants, so authoritative evidence is required.

notation.meaning: Event that the current random model satisfies both local accuracy inequalities.
Uniform lower bound on conditional model-accuracy probability.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: State-transition model lifecycle
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\). At iteration \(k\), let \(Z_k=(x_k,\Delta_k,m_k,D_k)\), where \(D_k\) is the derivative or sample information retained by the algorithm.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Abstract deterministic model-management family covering construction, reuse, validation, improvement, and replacement; it is not a convergence theorem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A model-lifecycle system is a state-transition map \[Z_{k+1}\in\mathcal T(Z_k,o_k),\] where \(o_k\) contains newly observed function or derivative information, together with a validity predicate \(V(Z_k,\delta)\). Its transitions are partitioned into: construction, which creates \(m_k\) from \(D_k\); reuse, which retains prior model information; validation, which evaluates \(V\); improvement, which changes \(D_k\) or \(m_k\) after failed validity; and replacement, which discards designated stale information. For every fixed \((x_k,\delta)\), repeated improvement transitions must terminate after finitely many steps at a state satisfying \[V(Z_k,\delta)=1\implies\sup_{\|x-x_k\|\leq\delta}|f(x)-m_k(x)|\leq\kappa\delta^2.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A model lifecycle is a state-transition system whose state contains the current point, radius, model, and retained derivative or sample data. Its allowed transitions construct, reuse, validate, improve, or replace model information. A declared validity predicate connects the management state to a uniform local fidelity bound. The essential termination condition is that, at a fixed center and radius, repeated improvement cannot continue indefinitely without producing a valid model.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A transition family is a model-lifecycle system when it supplies the stated state components, typed transitions, validity implication, and finite termination of model improvement at every fixed center and positive radius.
equivalent_formulations_latex: The lifecycle may be represented as a directed state graph whose improvement-only subgraph has no infinite path at fixed \((x_k,\delta)\).
special_cases_latex: A conditional interpolation lifecycle adds or exchanges sample points until the interpolation set is sufficiently poised.
A quasi-Newton lifecycle reuses \(H_k\) and replaces it by a secant update when the update denominator is admissible.
A memory lifecycle forms \(m_k=(1-\alpha_k)q_k+\alpha_km_{k-1}\).
immediate_consequences_latex: Validity and model construction are separate components: a syntactically defined model need not yet be certified adequate.
boundary_notes: The definition does not require every implementation to support every transition type.
The source supports the component mechanisms, but the unified state-transition packaging is a formal synthesis.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Decay of memory-model discrepancy after unsuccessful iterations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: The bound uses \kappa_t, the quantity defined in the theorem; this resolves the extract's inconsistent displayed subscript \kappa_k.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Assume the local models satisfy the stated global definition, twice-continuous differentiability, value-and-gradient agreement at x_i, and bounded-Hessian conditions. If iteration k is unsuccessful and t is the last successful iteration before k, then there exists \kappa_{\mathrm{mma}}>0 such that, for every x\in\mathcal B_k,
\[
|m_k(x)-q_k(x)|\le \kappa_{\mathrm{mma}}\,\kappa_t\,\alpha_{t,k}^{\,k-t},
\]
where
\[
\alpha_{t,k}:=\max_{i=t+1,\ldots,k}\alpha_i,
\qquad
\kappa_t:=\max_{\substack{i=0,\ldots,t+1\\x\in\mathcal B_{t+1}}}|q_i(x)|.
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under the local-model regularity and agreement conditions, if iteration k is unsuccessful and t is the preceding successful iteration, then throughout the current algorithmic region the memory model differs from the current local model by at most a constant times the maximum earlier model magnitude and the largest intervening memory weight raised to the number of intervening iterations.
assumptions_latex: t\text{ is the last successful iteration before }k
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \exists\kappa_{\mathrm{mma}}>0\ \forall x\in\mathcal B_k,\quad |m_k(x)-q_k(x)|\le\kappa_{\mathrm{mma}}\kappa_t\alpha_{t,k}^{k-t}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Eventual second-order fidelity of a memory model
knowledge_statements.scope_note: The named assumptions and radius-update rule are retained without supplying unstated definitions. The conclusion applies only when the unsuccessful iteration lies sufficiently far beyond its last successful predecessor.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Assume AM.10, AM.11, and AN.1. Suppose k is unsuccessful, the trust-region radius is updated according to (9.1.6), and t is the last successful iteration before k. Then there exist an integer \ell(t) and a constant \kappa_{\mathrm{cnd}} such that, if k\ge t+\ell(t),

\qquad\text{for every }x\in\mathcal B_k.
\]

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Decay condition for the memory parameter
knowledge_statements.scope_note: The bound applies after initialization; the separate condition \alpha_0=0 initializes the method without memory.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
There exist \bar\alpha\in[0,1), \psi>0, and \kappa_\alpha>0 satisfying
\[
\kappa_\alpha\left(\frac{\kappa_{\mathrm{une}}}{\gamma_1}\right)^\psi\le 1

\[
\alpha_k\le\min\left\{\bar\alpha,\kappa_\alpha\lVert s_{k-1}\rVert^\psi\right\},
\qquad \alpha_0=0.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: The zero-memory case recovers the current local model.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let q_k be the local model at iteration k. For a fixed \bar\alpha\in[0,1) and \alpha_k\in[0,\bar\alpha], define
\[
m_k(x)=(1-\alpha_k)q_k(x)+\alpha_km_{k-1}(x).
\]
If \alpha_k=0, then m_k=q_k.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A trust-region model with memory combines the current local model and the preceding model using a weight bounded strictly below one. A zero weight recovers the entirely local model.
assumptions_latex: q_k\text{ is the local model at iteration }k
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: m_k(x)=(1-\alpha_k)q_k(x)+\alpha_km_{k-1}(x),\qquad \alpha_k=0\Rightarrow m_k=q_k

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Regularity and first-order agreement of the local model
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Each q_k is defined on all of \mathbb R^n, while the uniform Hessian bound is asserted on \mathcal B_k.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For every k, q_k(x) is entirely determined by x_k and x and is defined for all x\in\mathbb R^n. Moreover, q_k\in C^2(\mathbb R^n),
\[
q_k(x_k)=f(x_k),\qquad \nabla q_k(x_k)=\nabla f(x_k),
\]
and, for every x\in\mathcal B_k,
\[
\lVert\nabla^2q_k(x)\rVert\le\kappa_{\mathrm{umh}}.
\]

children.title: Derivative-Model Lifecycle System
children.top_down_role: Curvature refresh, model reuse, replacement, and memory mechanisms.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.statement_title: Derivative-model refresh and memory system
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(m_k(x_k+s)=f_k+g_k^Ts+\tfrac12s^TH_ks\), with \(H_k=H_k^T\), and let \(s_k=x_{k+1}-x_k\), \(y_k=g_{k+1}-g_k\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Smooth finite-dimensional quadratic models managed through exact refresh, finite differences, quasi-Newton reuse, or limited memory.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A derivative-model lifecycle state is \(D_k=(g_k,H_k,\mathcal M_k)\), where \(\mathcal M_k\) stores selected correction data. A lifecycle transition chooses exactly one declared operation: \[\text{refresh: }(g_{k+1},H_{k+1})=(\nabla f(x_{k+1}),\nabla^2f(x_{k+1}));\] \[\text{difference: }(g_{k+1},H_{k+1})=(\bar g(x_{k+1},h_{k+1}),\bar H(x_{k+1},h_{k+1}));\] or \[\text{secant reuse: }H_{k+1}=U(H_k,s_k,y_k),\qquad H_{k+1}s_k=y_k,\] provided the selected update \(U\) is well defined. Limited-memory reuse retains only a prescribed number of low-rank correction pairs, while replacement clears \(\mathcal M_k\) and initializes a new base matrix.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A derivative-model lifecycle records the current gradient approximation, symmetric curvature approximation, and any retained correction pairs. Each transition is explicitly classified as an exact derivative refresh, finite-difference reconstruction, secant reuse, limited-memory update, or replacement. Secant reuse must satisfy the secant equation and may be performed only when the chosen formula is defined. A replacement discards the designated memory and installs a new base approximation.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \((D_k)\) is a derivative-model lifecycle precisely when every derivative-state change follows one of the declared refresh, difference, secant, limited-memory, or replacement operations with its domain conditions enforced.
equivalent_formulations_latex: A dense quasi-Newton lifecycle takes \(\mathcal M_k=\varnothing\) and stores the complete matrix \(H_k\); a limited-memory lifecycle represents \(H_k\) implicitly from a base matrix and retained correction pairs.
special_cases_latex: BFGS reuse requires \(y_k^Ts_k>0\) and preserves positive definiteness when initialized positive definite.
SR1 reuse requires \((y_k-H_ks_k)^Ts_k\neq0\).
immediate_consequences_latex: Low-rank secant reuse separates information retention from a complete derivative recomputation.
boundary_notes: Skipping an undefined update is distinct from asserting that the secant equation holds.
No convergence property follows solely from the lifecycle definition.

children.title: Derivative-Model Refresh
children.top_down_role: Policies for renewing derivative-based local model information.

knowledge_statements.title: Derivative-Model Refresh
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Recomputing derivative surrogates at the current center without changing their model class.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Input a current center \(x_k\), radius \(\Delta_k>0\), stored derivative model \((g_k,B_k)\), an error estimator \(E_k\), and tolerances \(\tau_g,tau_H\geq0\). If
\[
E_k^g>\tau_g\Delta_k
\quad\text{or}\quad
E_k^H>\tau_H,
\]
query the prescribed derivative or sampling oracle at \(x_k\), recompute \((g_k^+,B_k^+)\), symmetrize \(B_k^+\), and replace the stored timestamp and error estimates. Otherwise set \((g_k^+,B_k^+)=(g_k,B_k)\). Output the refreshed model
\[
m_k^+(s)=f_k+(g_k^+)^{\mathsf T}s+\tfrac12s^{\mathsf T}B_k^+s.
\]
A refresh changes numerical derivative information but preserves the selected model representation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: When derivative-error estimates exceed radius-scaled tolerances, recompute the stored gradient and Hessian surrogates and rebuild the same model class.
assumptions_latex: The derivative or sampling oracle returns finite estimates at \(x_k\).
The estimators \(E_k^g,E_k^H\) correspond to the stored derivative surrogates.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The output is either the unchanged model or a newly evaluated derivative model of the same representation class.
review_flags: Refresh triggers and tolerances are framework-dependent.
A lifecycle specification or algorithm source is required.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Algorithm is the correct role for a refresh operation, but the proposed thresholds are framework-dependent and are not derived from a cited lifecycle specification. The statement also uses the undefined token “tau_H” in place of \(\tau_H\). Source uncertainty prevents selecting a reliable corrected policy.

children.title: Derivative-Model Memory
children.top_down_role: Retention and reuse of curvature or derivative-model information across iterations.

knowledge_statements.title: Derivative-Model Memory
knowledge_statements.scope_note: State retained across iterations for reuse and validation of derivative surrogates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A derivative-model memory state at iteration \(k\) is a tuple
\[
\mathcal M_k=(\bar x_k,\bar\Delta_k,\bar g_k,\bar B_k,\varepsilon_k^g,\varepsilon_k^H,t_k),
\]
where \((\bar g_k,\bar B_k)\) are stored derivative surrogates constructed at center \(\bar x_k\) and scale \(\bar\Delta_k\), \((\varepsilon_k^g,\varepsilon_k^H)\) are certified or estimated error bounds, and \(t_k\) records provenance or age. The memory is admissible for a requested pair \((x,Delta)\) only when a declared reuse predicate \(R(mathcal M_k,x,Delta)=1\). Reuse returns the stored surrogates; failure of the predicate must invoke refresh or replacement rather than silently treating stale information as current.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Derivative-model memory stores surrogates, their center and scale, error metadata, and provenance; a declared predicate governs whether reuse is admissible.
assumptions_latex: The reuse predicate \(R\) is fixed before the stored model is assessed for the requested step.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Stored derivatives may be reused exactly when \(R(\mathcal M_k,x,\Delta)=1\).
review_flags: Derivative-model memory is an architectural interface rather than a uniquely standardized mathematical object.
A framework-specific lifecycle source is required.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Representation is a plausible role for retained model state, but this tuple and reuse contract are not standardized and lack a framework source. The statement also contains malformed occurrences of \(\Delta\) and \(\mathcal M_k\), which must be repaired once the intended interface is sourced.

children.title: Derivative-Model Replacement
children.top_down_role: Regimes for discarding stale or unreliable derivative-model information.

knowledge_statements.title: Derivative-Model Replacement
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Switching to a new derivative-model instance or representation after reuse becomes inadmissible.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Input the current state \((x_k,Delta_k,mathcal M_k)\), a finite collection of candidate model builders \(\{\mathcal B_j\}_{j\in J}\), and admissibility tests \(Q_j\). If the stored model fails its reuse test, choose an index \(j_k\in J\), construct
\[
(g_k^{\mathrm{new}},B_k^{\mathrm{new}},e_k^{\mathrm{new}})=\mathcal B_{j_k}(x_k,Delta_k),
\]
and accept it only if \(Q_{j_k}(e_k^{\mathrm{new}},Delta_k)=1\). On acceptance, discard the old active instance, initialize new provenance metadata, and output
\[
m_k^{\mathrm{new}}(s)=f_k+(g_k^{\mathrm{new}})^{\mathsf T}s+tfrac12s^{\mathsf T}B_k^{\mathrm{new}}s.
\]
If no candidate passes, report model-construction failure rather than returning an inadmissible model.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: When stored derivatives are inadmissible, build and validate a new model instance; replace the active model only after its acceptance test passes.
assumptions_latex: \(J\) is finite and every invoked builder terminates with an estimate or a failure report.
Each acceptance test \(Q_j\) is specified before construction.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The procedure outputs an accepted replacement model or an explicit model-construction failure.
review_flags: Replacement policy and acceptance tests depend on the surrounding lifecycle system.
A framework-specific algorithm source is required.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Algorithm is appropriate for the replacement leaf, but the builder selection and acceptance policy are framework-specific and unsupported. Multiple malformed TeX tokens, including the occurrences intended as \(\Delta_k\), \(\mathcal M_k\), and \(\tfrac12\), also require correction after the governing specification is identified.

children.title: Sample-Based Model Management
children.top_down_role: Interpolation and regression model adequacy, sample geometry, and geometry improvement.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.statement_title: Sample-based local-model management state
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\), let \(x_k\in\mathbb R^n\), and let \(Y_k\subset\mathbb R^n\) be a finite set at which values of \(f\) are available. Let \(\mathcal P\) be a finite-dimensional polynomial space.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Deterministic interpolation-based model management; noisy regression is acknowledged as a nearby variant but is not asserted by the cited source.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A sample-based model-management state is \((x_k,\Delta_k,Y_k,m_k)\) satisfying \[m_k(y)=f(y)\quad(y\in Y_k),\qquad Y_k\subseteq Q_k(\delta_k),\] where \(m_k\in\mathcal P\) is uniquely determined whenever the evaluation map \(E_{Y_k}:\mathcal P\to\mathbb R^{|Y_k|}\), \(E_{Y_k}p=(p(y))_{y\in Y_k}\), is nonsingular. The state is adequate when \(Y_k\) is poised and its fundamental polynomials are uniformly bounded on \(Q_k(\delta_k)\). A management transition may add, exchange, or delete sample points, but an accepted transition must retain known values and restore poisedness and locality before the model is certified valid.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A sample-based model-management state consists of a center, radius, finite sample set, and polynomial model interpolating all retained values. The interpolation model is uniquely defined when the evaluation map on the selected polynomial space is nonsingular. Adequacy additionally requires the samples to remain near the current center and the associated fundamental polynomials to be bounded over the model-validity ball. Updates may add, exchange, or remove points, but validity is certified only after geometry and locality have been restored.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The state is an adequate sample-based model state when interpolation holds, the evaluation map is nonsingular, the samples are local, and the fundamental-polynomial geometry bound holds on the validity ball.
equivalent_formulations_latex: For a basis \(\{\phi_j\}_{j=1}^p\) with \(|Y_k|=p\), poisedness is equivalent to \(\det[\phi_j(y_i)]_{i,j=1}^p\neq0\).
special_cases_latex: For full quadratic interpolation, \(p=(n+1)(n+2)/2\).
For a fully linear polynomial model, at least \(n+1\) suitably placed samples are required.
immediate_consequences_latex: Cardinality alone does not guarantee adequacy because a geometrically degenerate sample set can make the interpolation system singular.
boundary_notes: The definition does not cover least-squares regression with more observations than coefficients.
Poisedness ensures algebraic uniqueness; quantitative fidelity also depends on sample locality and geometry bounds.

notation.meaning: Polynomial evaluation map on the current sample set.

children.title: Sample-Fit Model Family
children.top_down_role: Sample-based local-model families distinguished by data sufficiency and noise handling.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.statement_title: Polynomial sample-interpolation model family
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(Y=\{y_1,\ldots,y_p\}\subset\mathbb R^n\), let observed values \(f(y_i)\) be available, and let \(\mathcal P=\operatorname{span}\{\phi_1,\ldots,\phi_p\}\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact, square polynomial interpolation models for smooth derivative-free optimization; noisy overdetermined regression is outside the sourced scope.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A sample-fit interpolation model is a polynomial \[m(x)=\sum_{j=1}^p\alpha_j\phi_j(x)\in\mathcal P\] whose coefficients satisfy \[\sum_{j=1}^p\alpha_j\phi_j(y_i)=f(y_i),\qquad i=1,\ldots,p.\] Let \(V(Y)=[\phi_j(y_i)]_{i,j=1}^p\). The fit is unisolvent, and hence defines one model for every data vector, exactly when \(\det V(Y)\neq0\). A local sample-fit family additionally requires \(Y\subseteq Q(x_c,\delta)\) and uses a degree or subspace declared in advance.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Choose a polynomial space with basis functions \(\phi_1,\ldots,\phi_p\) and the same number of sampled points. A sample-fit model is the polynomial whose coefficients solve the interpolation equations at those points. The model exists uniquely for every vector of sampled values exactly when the square evaluation matrix is nonsingular. A local family also declares its polynomial degree or subspace and confines the samples to a neighborhood of the model center.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The sample fit is uniquely defined if and only if \(V(Y)\) is nonsingular, in which case \(\alpha=V(Y)^{-1}(f(y_1),\ldots,f(y_p))^T\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: Unisolvence is equivalent to: the only \(p\in\mathcal P\) satisfying \(p(y_i)=0\) for every \(i\) is the zero polynomial.
For a Lagrange basis \(L_i\), the model is \(m(x)=\sum_{i=1}^pf(y_i)L_i(x)\) with \(L_i(y_j)=\delta_{ij}\).
special_cases_latex: Affine interpolation uses \(\mathcal P=\operatorname{span}\{1,x_1,\ldots,x_n\}\) and \(p=n+1\).
Full quadratic interpolation uses \(p=(n+1)(n+2)/2\).
immediate_consequences_latex: A set of the correct cardinality can still fail to define a unique model if its evaluation matrix is singular.
boundary_notes: Least-squares regression, regularized fitting, and stochastic observations require separate definitions.
Unisolvence alone does not bound the interpolation error unless geometric conditioning and sample locality are controlled.

notation.meaning: Square evaluation or interpolation matrix for the chosen basis and sample set.

children.title: Interpolation Models
children.top_down_role: Sample-based local models fitted to interpolate selected observations.

knowledge_statements.title: Interpolation Models
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact sample fitting in a prescribed finite-dimensional model space.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(Y=\{y^0,\ldots,y^{q-1}\}\subset\mathbb R^n\), let \(z_i=f(y^i)\), and let \(\mathcal P=\operatorname{span}\{\phi_0,\ldots,\phi_{q-1}\}\) be a \(q\)-dimensional function space. An interpolation model is a function
\[
m(y)=\sum_{j=0}^{q-1}\alpha_j\phi_j(y)
\]
whose coefficients satisfy \(m(y^i)=z_i\) for every \(i\in\{0,\ldots,q-1\}\). Define the interpolation matrix \(V\in\mathbb R^{q\times q}\) by \(V_{ij}=\phi_j(y^i)\). The interpolant exists uniquely exactly when \(V\) is nonsingular; in that case, \(\alpha=V^{-1}z\). For polynomial models, nonsingularity is the poisedness condition of the sample set for \(\mathcal P\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An interpolation model exactly matches every sample value in a chosen finite-dimensional model space and is unique precisely when its interpolation matrix is nonsingular.
assumptions_latex: The sample points \(y^0,\ldots,y^{q-1}\in\mathbb R^n\) are distinct.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A unique interpolant exists if and only if \(V\) is nonsingular, in which case \(\alpha=V^{-1}z\).

children.title: Regression Models
children.top_down_role: Sample-based local models fitted through overdetermined or noisy observations.

knowledge_statements.title: Regression Models
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Weighted least-squares fitting when samples need not be matched exactly.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let samples \((y^i,z_i)\) be given for \(i\in\{0,\ldots,N-1\}\), let \(w_i>0\), and let \(\mathcal P=\operatorname{span}\{\phi_0,\ldots,\phi_{q-1}\}\) with \(N\geq q\). A weighted regression model is
\[
m(y)=\sum_{j=0}^{q-1}\alpha_j\phi_j(y),
\qquad
\alpha\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{a\in\mathbb R^q}\sum_{i=0}^{N-1}w_i\left(\sum_{j=0}^{q-1}a_j\phi_j(y^i)-z_i\right)^2.
\]
Writing \(V_{ij}=\phi_j(y^i)\), \(W=\operatorname{diag}(w_0,\ldots,w_{N-1})\), and \(z=(z_0,\ldots,z_{N-1})^{\mathsf T}\), the coefficient vector is unique when \(V\in\mathbb R^{N\times q}\) has full column rank, and then
\[
\alpha=(V^{\mathsf T}WV)^{-1}V^{\mathsf T}Wz.
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A regression model minimizes weighted squared sample residuals in a chosen model space; full column rank of the sample design matrix makes its coefficient vector unique.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: If \(V\) has full column rank, the weighted least-squares model exists uniquely and has coefficient vector \(\alpha=(V^{\mathsf T}WV)^{-1}V^{\mathsf T}Wz\).
review_flags: No supplied locator specifically supports regression-based trust-region model fitting.

children.title: Sample-Fit Regime Selection
children.top_down_role: Data-sufficiency and noise regimes governing interpolation or regression use.

knowledge_statements.title: Sample-Fit Regime Selection
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Selects interpolation or regression from sample count and normalized design-matrix geometry.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\phi=(\phi_1,\ldots,\phi_q)\) be a model basis and let \(Y=\{y^1,\ldots,y^p\}\) be sampled points with values \(f_Y\). Form the normalized design matrix \(A_{ij}=\phi_j(y^i)\). If \(p=q\) and \(A\) is nonsingular with an acceptable geometry diagnostic, choose interpolation and solve \(A\alpha=f_Y\). If \(p>q\) and \(A\) has full column rank, choose regression and compute \(\alpha\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{a\in\mathbb R^q}\|Aa-f_Y\|_2^2\). If neither condition holds, declare geometry repair or regularization necessary; do not accept an unregularized sample-fit model.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Use well-conditioned square sampling for interpolation, overdetermined full-rank sampling for regression, and repair or regularize rank-deficient designs.
assumptions_latex: \(p\ge q\) whenever an unregularized fit is requested.
All basis functions are defined at every point of \(Y\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\text{regime}\in\{\text{interpolation},\text{regression},\text{repair-or-regularize}\}\) is selected by the rank and dimensions of \(A\).
review_flags: A sample-based model-management source with an exact interpolation-versus-regression selection rule is required.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm fits the leaf, but the exact interpolation-versus-regression decision rule is uncited and leaves the acceptable geometry diagnostic undefined. An authoritative sample-based model-management source is required before the rule can be assessed reliably.

children.title: Sample-Geometry Quality System
children.top_down_role: Sample-set quality and model-repair families supporting reliable local approximation.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.statement_title: Poised sample geometry and geometry repair
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(\mathcal P\) be a \(p\)-dimensional polynomial space, \(Y=\{y_1,\ldots,y_p\}\subset Q(x_c,\delta)\), and let \(L_1,\ldots,L_p\in\mathcal P\) be the Lagrange fundamental polynomials when they exist.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact interpolation geometry in a finite-dimensional polynomial space, including qualitative poisedness and a quantitative bounded-basis criterion.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The set \(Y\) is poised for \(\mathcal P\) if the evaluation map \(E_Y:\mathcal P\to\mathbb R^p\) is bijective, equivalently if unique polynomials \(L_i\in\mathcal P\) satisfy \(L_i(y_j)=\delta_{ij}\). It is \(\Lambda\)-poised in \(Q(x_c,\delta)\) if, additionally, \[\max_{1\leq i\leq p}\sup_{x\in Q(x_c,\delta)}|L_i(x)|\leq\Lambda.\] A geometry-improvement operation replaces or adds sample points so that the resulting set is contained in the ball and satisfies the selected nonzero-pivot or \(\Lambda\)-poised condition.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A sample set is poised for a polynomial space when evaluation on that set determines every polynomial coefficient uniquely. Equivalently, a complete Lagrange basis exists. Quantitative geometry quality is obtained by bounding every fundamental polynomial throughout the model-validity ball. A geometry-repair operation changes sample points until the set is local and meets the chosen nonsingularity or bounded-basis threshold.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(Y\) has certified geometry quality on \(Q(x_c,\delta)\) when it is poised and its fundamental polynomials satisfy the stated uniform \(\Lambda\) bound there.
equivalent_formulations_latex: For any basis \(\{\phi_j\}\) of \(\mathcal P\), poisedness is equivalent to \(\det[\phi_j(y_i)]\neq0\).
In a Newton-basis construction, qualitative poisedness is equivalent to every interpolation pivot being nonzero.
special_cases_latex: A well-poised Newton construction enforces a positive lower pivot threshold rather than merely nonzero pivots.
For affine models, poisedness means that the \(n+1\) points are affinely independent.
immediate_consequences_latex: Poisedness ensures uniqueness of interpolation; \(\Lambda\)-poisedness also controls amplification by the interpolation basis.
boundary_notes: A nonzero determinant without a quantitative bound may still describe severely ill-conditioned geometry.
The numerical value of \(\Lambda\) depends on the region and the selected polynomial space.

notation.meaning: Uniform bound on the magnitudes of the fundamental polynomials over the model region.
Lagrange fundamental polynomial associated with sample point y_i.

children.title: Sample-Set Poisedness
children.top_down_role: Geometric quality regimes for sample sets supporting local model construction.

knowledge_statements.title: Sample-Set Poisedness
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines quantitative poisedness for polynomial interpolation on a trust region.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal P\) be a \(q\)-dimensional polynomial space, let \(Y=\{y^1,\ldots,y^q\}\subset\mathbb R^n\), and let \(D=B(x,\Delta)\). The set \(Y\) is poised for interpolation in \(\mathcal P\) when evaluation on \(Y\) is unisolvent, equivalently when unique Lagrange polynomials \(\ell_1,\ldots,\ell_q\in\mathcal P\) satisfy \(\ell_i(y^j)=\delta_{ij}\). For \(\Lambda\ge1\), the set is \(\Lambda\)-poised in \(D\) when, additionally, \[\max_{1\le i\le q}\ \sup_{z\in D}|\ell_i(z)|\le\Lambda.\] Smaller admissible \(\Lambda\) represents better interpolation geometry over the trust region.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A sample set is Lambda-poised when interpolation is unique and every Lagrange polynomial stays uniformly bounded by Lambda throughout the trust region.
assumptions_latex: \(\Delta>0\) and \(Y\) contains exactly \(q=\dim\mathcal P\) distinct points.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(Y\) is \(\Lambda\)-poised in \(B(x,\Delta)\) precisely when it is unisolvent and its Lagrange basis obeys the displayed bound.

knowledge_statements.title: Geometry Improvement
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Lagrange-polynomial exchange procedure for improving interpolation geometry.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a poised interpolation set \(Y=\{y^1,\ldots,y^q\}\), its Lagrange basis \(\{\ell_i\}_{i=1}^q\), a region \(D=B(x,\Delta)\), and a target \(\Lambda\ge1\), compute \(M_i=\sup_{z\in D}|\ell_i(z)|\). If \(\max_i M_i\le\Lambda\), return \(Y\). Otherwise choose \(j\in\operatorname*{argmax}_i M_i\), select \(z_j\in D\) attaining or sufficiently approximating \(M_j\), evaluate the objective at \(z_j\), and replace \(y^j\) by \(z_j\). Recompute the interpolation basis and repeat until the target is met or an evaluation budget is exhausted.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Replace the point associated with the largest Lagrange-polynomial excursion by a maximizing trust-region point until poisedness is acceptable or the budget ends.
assumptions_latex: The initial set is poised for the chosen polynomial space.
Each required maximization over \(D\) is solved exactly or to a prescribed approximation tolerance.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The output is either a set satisfying \(\max_i\sup_{z\in D}|\ell_i(z)|\le\Lambda\) or a declared budget-limited failure.

knowledge_statements.title: Geometry Repair Triggers
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Diagnostic conditions that require sample-set repair before model acceptance.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For an interpolation set \(Y\) on \(D=B(x,\\Delta)\), let \(\ell_i\) be its Lagrange polynomials and let \(\widetilde A\) be the design matrix after translating by \(x\) and scaling coordinates by \(\Delta\). Given thresholds \(\Lambda_{\max}\ge1\) and \(\tau>0\), trigger geometry repair whenever \[Y\text{ is not unisolvent},\qquad \max_i\sup_{z\in D}|\ell_i(z)|>\Lambda_{\max},\qquad\text{or}\qquad \sigma_{\min}(\widetilde A)<\tau.\] The first test is definitive; the latter two are quantitative instability tests. Model acceptance may resume only after the selected diagnostic satisfies its prescribed threshold.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Repair is triggered by nonunique interpolation, excessive Lagrange growth, or an inadequately small singular value of the normalized design matrix.
assumptions_latex: \(\Delta>0\), and all geometry thresholds are fixed before applying the acceptance test.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: If any displayed predicate holds, the current sample geometry is rejected and a repair step is required.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.statement_title: Quadratic trust-region subproblem
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(g\in\mathbb R^n\), \(H=H^T\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}\), \(\Delta>0\), and let \(\|\cdot\|_{\mathcal R}\) be a norm on \(\mathbb R^n\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional, possibly nonconvex quadratic minimization over a closed norm ball; the Euclidean case is distinguished when optimality multipliers are discussed.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The trust-region subproblem associated with \((g,H,\Delta,\|\cdot\|_{\mathcal R})\) is \[v_{\mathrm{TR}}=\min_{s\in\mathbb R^n}\left\{q(s)=g^Ts+\tfrac12s^THs:\ \|s\|_{\mathcal R}\leq\Delta\right\}.\] Its solution set is \(S_{\mathrm{TR}}=\operatorname*{argmin}_{\|s\|_{\mathcal R}\leq\Delta}q(s)\). A vector \(s_*\) is a global trust-region step exactly when \(s_*\in S_{\mathrm{TR}}\); an approximate trust-region step must be separately qualified by a declared decrease or residual certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Given a linear term \(g\), symmetric curvature matrix \(H\), positive radius \(\Delta\), and region norm, the trust-region subproblem minimizes the quadratic \(q(s)=g^Ts+\tfrac12s^THs\) over the corresponding closed ball. Its value is \(v_{\mathrm{TR}}\), and its global solution set contains all feasible steps attaining that value. Approximate steps are not solutions by definition unless a separate quality criterion is supplied.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(S_{\mathrm{TR}}=\{s:\|s\|_{\mathcal R}\leq\Delta,\ q(s)=v_{\mathrm{TR}}\}\) is the trust-region subproblem solution set.
equivalent_formulations_latex: Adding a constant \(f(x)\) to \(q\) changes the optimal value by that constant but leaves \(S_{\mathrm{TR}}\) unchanged.
For an ellipsoidal region \(\|S^{-1}s\|_2\leq\Delta\) with nonsingular \(S\), the substitution \(s=Sw\) gives a Euclidean-ball quadratic in \(w\).
special_cases_latex: The standard spherical subproblem uses \(\|\cdot\|_{\mathcal R}=\|\cdot\|_2\).
Box trust regions use \(\|s\|_\infty\leq\Delta\).
If \(H\succeq0\), the objective is convex; if \(H\) is indefinite, every global minimizer lies on the boundary.
immediate_consequences_latex: A global minimizer exists because the feasible norm ball is nonempty and compact and \(q\) is continuous.
boundary_notes: The subproblem definition does not require uniqueness.
A local minimizer of an indefinite quadratic need not be a global trust-region solution.

notation.meaning: Optimal value of the trust-region subproblem.
Set of global trust-region subproblem minimizers.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Geometry-curvature-activity taxonomy for trust-region subproblems
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Consider \(\min\{g^Ts+\tfrac12s^THs:\|s\|_{\mathcal R}\leq\Delta\}\), with \(H=H^T\), \(\Delta>0\), and a global minimizer \(s_*\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A classification of finite-dimensional quadratic trust-region instances and their global solutions, not an assertion that all classes have equal computational complexity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The regime label of an instance-solution pair is the triple \(R=(R_{\mathrm{geom}},R_{\mathrm{curv}},R_{\mathrm{act}})\), where \[R_{\mathrm{geom}}=\begin{cases}\mathrm{spherical},&\|s\|_{\mathcal R}=\|s\|_2,\\ \mathrm{ellipsoidal},&\|s\|_{\mathcal R}=\|S^{-1}s\|_2\text{ for nonsingular }S,\\ \mathrm{nonEuclidean},&\text{otherwise},\end{cases}\] \[R_{\mathrm{curv}}=\begin{cases}\mathrm{positive\ definite},&H\succ0,\\ \mathrm{positive\ semidefinite\ singular},&H\succeq0,\ \ker H\neq\{0\},\\ \mathrm{indefinite},&\lambda_{\min}(H)<0,\end{cases}\] and \(R_{\mathrm{act}}=\mathrm{interior}\) if \(\|s_*\|_{\mathcal R}<\Delta\), otherwise \(R_{\mathrm{act}}=\mathrm{boundary}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Each quadratic trust-region instance together with a selected global solution receives three labels. The geometry label distinguishes a Euclidean ball, an invertibly scaled Euclidean ellipsoid, and any other norm geometry. The curvature label distinguishes positive-definite, singular positive-semidefinite, and indefinite Hessians. The activity label records whether the selected global minimizer lies strictly inside the region or on its boundary.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The taxonomy map assigns the unique geometry and curvature labels determined by the data and the activity label determined by \(s_*\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: In the Euclidean case, boundary activity is \(\|s_*\|_2=\Delta\), while interior activity is \(\|s_*\|_2<\Delta\).
special_cases_latex: Every indefinite instance has boundary global solutions.
A positive-definite instance is interior exactly when its unconstrained minimizer \(-H^{-1}g\) lies strictly inside the region.
immediate_consequences_latex: Different global minimizers of a singular convex instance may have different activity labels, so activity belongs to the instance-solution pair rather than only to \((g,H,\Delta)\).
boundary_notes: The three labels do not encode hard-case orthogonality or numerical conditioning.
A polyhedral norm is non-Euclidean under this taxonomy even when its unit ball is linearly transformed.

notation.meaning: Spectral curvature class of the quadratic Hessian.
Interior or boundary status of a selected global solution.
