children.title: Criticality Measure Diagnostics
children.top_down_role: Assessment of computed criticality measures used to support termination decisions.

knowledge_statements.title: Criticality Measure Diagnostics
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Diagnostic consistency checks for a model-based first-order criticality measure.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For unconstrained minimization with differentiable model \(m_k\), define \(\chi_k=\|
abla m_k(0)\|\). If the model is first-order consistent, \(
abla m_k(0)=
abla f(x_k)\), then \(\chi_k\leq\varepsilon_g\) certifies \(\varepsilon_g\)-first-order stationarity. If only \(\|
abla f(x_k)-
abla m_k(0)\|\leq\kappa_g\Delta_k\) is known, then the verifiable implication is \[\|
abla f(x_k)\|\leq\chi_k+\kappa_g\Delta_k.\] Consequently, termination based on \(\chi_k\) is justified only when both \(\chi_k\) and the model-error term are below allocated tolerances. A diagnostic must flag nonfinite values, inconsistent scaling, or a criticality measure small solely because \(\Delta_k\) is small.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Model criticality certifies true stationarity only with derivative consistency or an explicit model-gradient error allowance.
assumptions_latex: The objective and model are differentiable at the current iterate.
A derivative-matching identity or a certified model-gradient error bound is available.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The true gradient obeys \(\|\nabla f(x_k)\|\leq\chi_k+\kappa_g\Delta_k\), yielding a checkable termination certificate.

children.title: False Termination Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Situations where inaccurate models or evaluations create premature stopping signals.

knowledge_statements.title: False Termination Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Concrete mechanisms by which small-step or small-model-gradient tests falsely report convergence.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Neither a small accepted step nor a small trust-region radius implies stationarity. For \(f(x)=x\) on \(\mathbb{R}\), \(
abla f(x)=1\) everywhere, yet a radius sequence \(\Delta_k\downarrow0\) forces every feasible trial step to satisfy \(|s_k|\leq\Delta_k	o0\). Thus any rule terminating solely because \(\|s_k\|\leq\varepsilon_x\) or \(\Delta_k\leq\varepsilon_\Delta\) can declare convergence at a nonstationary point. Likewise, an inaccurate model with \(
abla m_k(0)=0\) may produce zero model criticality while \(
abla f(x_k)
eq0\). False termination is excluded only by checking a reliable objective criticality measure or a model measure accompanied by a certified derivative-error bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Tiny steps, tiny radii, or a zero gradient from an inaccurate model can occur far from stationarity and cannot alone justify convergence.
assumptions_latex: A stopping rule uses only step size, radius, or an uncertified model criticality measure.
No reliable objective-gradient or derivative-error check is imposed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Such a stopping rule may terminate with \(\|\nabla f(x_k)\|>0\), as shown by \(f(x)=x\) with \(\Delta_k\downarrow0\).

children.title: Progress-Stagnation Diagnostics
children.top_down_role: Indicators distinguishing genuine stationarity from stalled computational progress.

knowledge_statements.title: Progress-Stagnation Diagnostics
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Windowed diagnostic separating insufficient objective progress from approximate first-order termination.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For accepted iterates \(x_k\), define actual decrease \(a_k=f(x_k)-f(x_{k+1})\) and a first-order criticality measure \(\chi_k\ge 0\). Given a window length \(w\in\mathbb N\), progress tolerance \(\tau_f>0\), and stationarity tolerance \(\varepsilon_g>0\), declare progress stagnation at iteration \(k\ge w\) when
\[
\sum_{j=k-w}^{k-1}\max\{a_j,0\}\le \tau_f\max\{1,|f(x_{k-w})|\}
\quad\text{and}\quad
\max_{k-w\le j\le k}\chi_j>\varepsilon_g.
\]
The second inequality excludes legitimate termination: small accumulated decrease alone is not evidence of stagnation when every recent iterate is approximately stationary.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Stagnation occurs when accepted iterations produce negligible cumulative decrease over a fixed window while at least one recent criticality measure remains above tolerance.
assumptions_latex: \(f(x_j)\) and \(\chi_j\) are finite for the inspected iterations.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\sum_{j=k-w}^{k-1}\max\{a_j,0\}\le \tau_f\max\{1,|f(x_{k-w})|\}\) together with \(\max_{k-w\le j\le k}\chi_j>\varepsilon_g\) diagnoses nonstationary progress stagnation.

notation.meaning: Actual objective decrease on accepted iteration k.

source_refs.locator: 6.1 The Basic Trust-Region Algorithm p. 115

children.title: Inner-Outer Accuracy Coordination
children.top_down_role: Coordination of subproblem effort with model quality and outer progress.

knowledge_statements.title: Inner-Outer Accuracy Coordination
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Forcing-rule coordination for an inexact solution of each trust-region subproblem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(m_k(p)=f_k+g_k^{T}p+\tfrac12p^{T}B_kp\) on \(\|p\|\le\Delta_k\), and let \(p_k^C\) be a Cauchy step. The inner solver is sufficiently accurate for the outer iteration if it returns a feasible \(p_k\) satisfying
\[
m_k(0)-m_k(p_k)\ge \kappa_s\bigl(m_k(0)-m_k(p_k^C)\bigr),\qquad \kappa_s\in(0,1].
\]
Additional inner refinement should be required only when this decrease test or a prescribed subproblem residual test fails. Thus inner accuracy is tightened as outer criticality and model reliability improve, while computation beyond the accuracy needed to determine the outer acceptance decision is avoided.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Solve each subproblem only accurately enough to secure a fixed fraction of Cauchy decrease and any required residual accuracy, tightening effort near reliable stationary regimes.
assumptions_latex: The Cauchy step \(p_k^C\) is feasible and has nonnegative predicted decrease.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(p_k\) supplies sufficient inner accuracy when \(\|p_k\|\le\Delta_k\) and its predicted decrease is at least the fraction \(\kappa_s\) of Cauchy decrease.

notation.meaning: Quadratic trust-region model at the outer iterate.
Cauchy step for the model and radius.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The fixed fraction-of-Cauchy-decrease test is standard, but it does not itself express the asserted tightening of inner accuracy with outer criticality and model reliability. The claims about residual refinement and avoiding work beyond the acceptance decision require a specific inexact-solve or forcing-rule source.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.statement_title: Inner–outer accuracy coordination rule
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: At outer iteration \(k\), let the trust-region model be \(m_k\), let \(g_k=\nabla m_k(x_k)\), let \(\Delta_k>0\), and let \(\beta_k>0\) bound model curvature. An inner solver returns \(s_k\) and reports an inner residual or effort count.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: The rule coordinates deterministic approximate solution of a smooth trust-region subproblem with outer progress. It does not prescribe a particular inner solver.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: An inner–outer accuracy coordination rule is a forcing policy that accepts an inner step only if it is trust-region feasible and achieves a reduction commensurate with the outer criticality and radius. A canonical condition is \(\|s_k\|_k\leq\kappa_{\mathrm{tr}}\Delta_k\) and \(m_k(x_k)-m_k(x_k+s_k)\geq\kappa_{\mathrm{mdc}}\|g_k\|\min\{\|g_k\|/\beta_k,\Delta_k\}\), where \(\kappa_{\mathrm{mdc}}>0\) and \(\kappa_{\mathrm{tr}}\geq1\) are fixed. If an exact model minimizer \(s_k^M\) exists, an alternative relative rule requires \(m_k(x_k)-m_k(x_k+s_k)\geq\kappa_{\mathrm{amm}}[m_k(x_k)-m_k(x_k+s_k^M)]\). The policy may tighten the inner residual tolerance as outer criticality decreases, but it stops inner work once one of these sufficient-reduction certificates holds unless extra inner accuracy has a declared evaluation-cost benefit.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The inner solver need not solve the subproblem exactly. Its result is adequate when the step is feasible and its predicted decrease is at least a fixed fraction of the Cauchy-scale decrease, or a fixed fraction of the optimal model decrease when that quantity exists. Accuracy may increase near outer criticality, but additional work after a certificate is obtained is classified as optional rather than necessary.
assumptions_latex: The model decrease can be evaluated reliably.
The constants \(\kappa_{\mathrm{mdc}},\kappa_{\mathrm{amm}}\) are positive and independent of \(k\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\|s_k\|_k\leq\kappa_{\mathrm{tr}}\Delta_k,\qquad m_k(x_k)-m_k(x_k+s_k)\geq\kappa_{\mathrm{mdc}}\|g_k\|\min\left\{\frac{\|g_k\|}{\beta_k},\Delta_k\right\}.\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: If \(s_k^M\) exists, a fixed fraction of optimal model reduction implies a Cauchy-type sufficient-decrease condition under the standard model assumptions.
For a quadratic Euclidean subproblem, feasibility may be relaxed to \(\|s_k\|_2\leq\kappa_{\mathrm{tr}}\Delta_k\) with a declared \(\kappa_{\mathrm{tr}}>1\).
special_cases_latex: A truncated conjugate-gradient solver may stop at the trust-region boundary, on negative curvature, or after attaining the required model reduction.
When objective evaluations dominate inner linear algebra, a stricter inner tolerance may be selected to reduce outer evaluations.
immediate_consequences_latex: Failure of the sufficient-decrease inequality is an inner-solver failure, not evidence of poor objective-model agreement.
Once the forcing condition holds, exact subproblem minimization is unnecessary for the basic outer acceptance test.
boundary_notes: An exact-minimizer relative rule is unsuitable in infinite-dimensional settings where the infimum may not be attained.
Oversolving is cost-relative: additional inner accuracy is not a mathematical failure unless it violates a declared effort policy.

notation.meaning: Required fraction in the Cauchy-scale decrease condition.
Positive curvature bound used in the decrease scale.
Exact model-minimizing step when it exists.

children.title: Trust-Region Fault-Isolation Diagnostics
children.top_down_role: Diagnostic families for identifying model, scaling, and subproblem-solver defects.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.statement_title: Trust-region fault-isolation signature
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(A_k=f(x_k)-f(x_k+s_k)\), \(P_k=m_k(x_k)-m_k(x_k+s_k)\), \(\rho_k=A_k/P_k\) when \(P_k>0\), and let \(C_k=\|s_k\|_k-\Delta_k\). Let \(Q_k\) denote the required Cauchy-scale decrease and let \(N_k\) denote a numerical-noise bound for forming \(A_k\) and \(P_k\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: This is a symptom-based deterministic isolation scheme. It identifies mutually testable fault classes but does not claim unique physical causation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A trust-region fault-isolation diagnostic is a classification map from an iteration record to a set of fault labels. It assigns a subproblem-feasibility fault when \(C_k>\tau_C\); an insufficient-solve fault when \(P_k<\kappa Q_k\); a model-agreement fault when \(P_k\geq\kappa Q_k\), \(\max\{|A_k|,|P_k|\}>N_k\), and \(|\rho_k-1|>\tau_\rho\); a numerical-resolution fault when \(\max\{|A_k|,|P_k|\}\leq N_k\); and a scaling or region fault when repeated rejected steps coexist with a severe mismatch between \(\|s_k\|_k\), \(\Delta_k\), and the scaled criticality measure. Multiple labels may be returned. The isolation is logically ordered so that an undefined or unreliable \(\rho_k\) is not used to diagnose model quality.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The classifier first checks whether the inner solver returned a feasible step and enough predicted decrease. It next checks whether the reductions are large enough to resolve numerically. Only then does it interpret a poor actual-to-predicted ratio as a model-agreement fault. Persistent rejection combined with inappropriate scaled step and radius sizes is reported separately as a scaling or region-control fault. Several labels may be active at once.
assumptions_latex: The thresholds \(\tau_C,\tau_\rho\) and \(\kappa\) are fixed and positive.
\(N_k\) bounds the resolution below which reduction comparisons are not trusted.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\mathcal F_k\subseteq\{\mathrm{feasibility},\mathrm{insufficient\ solve},\mathrm{model\ agreement},\mathrm{numerical\ resolution},\mathrm{scaling/region}\}\] is determined by the stated residual predicates.
equivalent_formulations_latex: The classifier may be expressed as a decision tree with numerical resolution checked before ratio-based model diagnosis.
The output may be a multi-hot fault vector rather than a set of labels.
special_cases_latex: If \(P_k\leq0\), the iteration is classified as a model/subproblem defect and \(\rho_k\) is not evaluated.
If both reductions are at roundoff scale, a computed negative ratio is classified as unresolved rather than as reliable disagreement.
immediate_consequences_latex: A poor ratio following an inadequate inner solve is not isolated as a pure model fault.
Direct computation of a quadratic model difference reduces cancellation-based false diagnoses.
boundary_notes: The labels are diagnostic equivalence classes, not proofs of root cause.
Threshold selection depends on scaling, arithmetic, and oracle accuracy.

source_refs.locator: Sections 17.4.1–17.4.4, especially direct model-decrease computation, unreliable rho_k near termination, stopping diagnostics, and noise safeguards, pp. 825–831

children.title: Scaling Diagnostics
children.top_down_role: Tests revealing harmful variable, objective, or trust-region scaling.

knowledge_statements.title: Scaling Diagnostics
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Coordinate-scaling checks for the model gradient and trust-region geometry.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Represent physical steps as \(p=D_ks\), where \(D_k\) is nonsingular and the scaled trust region is \(\|s\|\le\Delta_k\). The corresponding scaled gradient is \(D_k^{T}g_k\). Given limits \(K_D>1\) and \(K_g>1\), flag a scaling defect if
\[
\kappa_2(D_k)>K_D
\quad\text{or}\quad
\frac{\max_i |(D_k^{T}g_k)_i|}{\max\{\min_{i: (D_k^{T}g_k)_i\ne0}|(D_k^{T}g_k)_i|,\epsilon\}}>K_g,
\]
where \(\epsilon>0\) prevents division by zero. The diagnostic distinguishes anisotropy introduced by coordinates from poor agreement caused by the model or subproblem solver.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Flag scaling when the coordinate transformation is excessively ill-conditioned or produces scaled-gradient components with an extreme nonzero dynamic range.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Either displayed inequality is a scaling-warning predicate for iteration \(k\).

notation.meaning: Map from scaled coordinates to physical step coordinates.
Spectral condition number of the scaling map.

children.title: Model Adequacy Diagnostics
children.top_down_role: Tests distinguishing locally credible models from persistently poor approximations.

knowledge_statements.title: Model Adequacy Diagnostics
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Fully linear error tests on the current trust region, with the model expressed in step coordinates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\) be continuously differentiable on \(B(x_k,\Delta_k)\), and let \(m_k:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\) be continuously differentiable on \(B(0,\Delta_k)\). For constants \(\kappa_f,\kappa_g>0\), the model passes the local adequacy diagnostic when
\[
\sup_{\|p\|\le\Delta_k}|f(x_k+p)-m_k(p)|\le\kappa_f\Delta_k^2
\]
and
\[
\sup_{\|p\|\le\Delta_k}\|\nabla f(x_k+p)-\nabla m_k(p)\|\le\kappa_g\Delta_k.
\]
Violation of either bound flags inadequate local fidelity at the current radius. If implementations replace the suprema by sampled or validation-point estimates, the resulting test is only an empirical diagnostic.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A step-coordinate model is locally adequate when its value error is quadratic and its gradient error is linear in the trust-region radius throughout the corresponding physical and step-space balls.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) is continuously differentiable on \(B(x_k,\Delta_k)\), and \(m_k\) is continuously differentiable on \(B(0,\Delta_k)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The two displayed bounds certify fully linear model accuracy on the current trust region; violation of either bound diagnoses inadequate local fidelity.

notation.meaning: Closed physical-space trust-region ball centered at the current iterate.
Closed ball of admissible step vectors.

children.title: Subproblem Solver Diagnostics
children.top_down_role: Checks for insufficient subproblem progress, instability, or curvature-handling defects.

knowledge_statements.title: Subproblem Solver Diagnostics
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Feasibility and sufficient-decrease certificate for a computed trust-region step.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(m_k(p)=f_k+g_k^Tp+\tfrac12p^TB_kp\) with symmetric \(B_k\), define the Cauchy benchmark
\[
C_k=\tfrac12\|g_k\|\min\left\{\Delta_k,\frac{\|g_k\|}{\max\{\|B_k\|,\epsilon\}}\right\}.
\]
A computed step \(p_k\) passes the basic solver diagnostic if
\[
\|p_k\|\le(1+\tau_\Delta)\Delta_k,
\qquad m_k(0)-m_k(p_k)\ge\kappa_s C_k,
\]
where \(\tau_\Delta\ge0\), \(\kappa_s\in(0,1]\), and \(\epsilon>0\). Failure of feasibility implicates constraint handling; failure of sufficient decrease implicates premature termination, numerical instability, or missed descent or negative-curvature directions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A subproblem step is certified when it respects the radius within tolerance and achieves a fixed fraction of a standard Cauchy decrease bound.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The displayed feasibility and decrease inequalities form a directly checkable certificate of basic subproblem-solver adequacy.

children.title: Cross-Diagnostic Fault Isolation
children.top_down_role: Use of multiple diagnostic signals to localize the source of degraded performance.

knowledge_statements.title: Cross-Diagnostic Fault Isolation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Deterministic isolation rule combining scaling, model, and solver indicators.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
At iteration \(k\), compute Boolean indicators \(S_k\), \(M_k\), and \(Q_k\), respectively denoting failed scaling, model-adequacy, and subproblem-solver tests. Assign the fault label by
\[
L_k=
\begin{cases}
\text{scaling},&S_k\wedge\neg M_k\wedge\neg Q_k,\\
\text{model},&M_k\wedge\neg Q_k,\\
\text{solver},&Q_k\wedge\neg M_k,\\
\text{coupled},&(M_k\wedge Q_k)\vee(S_k\wedge(M_k\vee Q_k)),\\
\text{unresolved},&\neg S_k\wedge\neg M_k\wedge\neg Q_k.
\end{cases}
\]
On a coupled label, first normalize scaling, recompute the model test, and then rerun the solver test. Output the first label that remains invariant under this controlled recomputation; otherwise output unresolved.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Combine independent scaling, model, and solver tests; isolate a unique failed subsystem when possible and use controlled recomputation for coupled failures.
assumptions_latex: Controlled recomputation changes only the subsystem currently being tested.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The algorithm outputs \(L_k\in\{\text{scaling},\text{model},\text{solver},\text{coupled},\text{unresolved}\}\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The deterministic labeling table and controlled-recomputation rule are bespoke fault-isolation algorithms. No source is supplied for their exclusivity, ordering, or invariance criterion, so their reliability cannot be established.

children.title: Trust-Region Failure Regimes
children.top_down_role: Characteristic failures arising from model inadequacy, subproblem solution, region management, scaling, or oracle quality.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.statement_title: Trust-region failure regime taxonomy
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Consider a trust-region run \(\{x_k,m_k,s_k,\Delta_k,A_k,P_k,\rho_k\}_{k\geq0}\), with \(P_k>0\) whenever \(\rho_k\) is used. Let \(Q_k\) be the required model-decrease benchmark, \(N_k\) an evaluation-resolution bound, and \(\mathcal U=\{k:\rho_k<\eta_1\}\) the unsuccessful indices.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A failure regime is a formally specified persistent symptom of an execution, not merely one unsuccessful iteration and not necessarily a convergence theorem violation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A trust-region failure regime is an infinite or diagnostically long index set \(K\subseteq\mathbb N\) on which at least one of the following predicates persists: model inadequacy, \(P_k>0\), \(\max\{|A_k|,|P_k|\}>N_k\), and \(|\rho_k-1|>\tau_\rho\); subproblem failure, \(\|s_k\|_k>\Delta_k+\tau_s\) or \(P_k<\kappa Q_k\); region-control failure, the prescribed radius-update inclusion is violated or \(\Delta_k\) collapses while criticality remains above tolerance; or evaluation-reliability failure, \(\max\{|A_k|,|P_k|\}\leq N_k\) or derivative/model errors exceed their declared accuracy budgets. The taxonomy of a run is the multi-label set of predicates holding on each maximal contiguous or recurrent index set \(K\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A failure regime is a persistent, mathematically testable pattern across iterations. The principal classes are unreliable model agreement, inadequate or infeasible subproblem solutions, defective radius control, and reductions or derivatives that cannot be resolved to their claimed accuracy. A run may occupy several regimes simultaneously, and a single rejected step alone is not a regime.
assumptions_latex: All thresholds and accuracy budgets are fixed before classifying the run.
The predicted reduction is computed independently of the objective reduction.
Persistence is defined by a declared window length or by infinitely many occurrences.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\mathfrak R(K)\subseteq\{\mathrm{model},\mathrm{subproblem},\mathrm{region},\mathrm{evaluation}\},\qquad \mathfrak R(K)\neq\varnothing.\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: A regime may be represented by a maximal interval on which a fault predicate holds, or by a recurrent subsequence with the same predicate.
The taxonomy is multi-label because model, region, and evaluation defects need not be mutually exclusive.
special_cases_latex: Repeated ordinary rejection with correct contraction is not itself a region-control failure.
A ratio anomaly at the noise floor belongs to the evaluation class rather than automatically to the model class.
immediate_consequences_latex: Every classified failure carries an explicit measurable witness.
The taxonomy separates the object being diagnosed from the algorithmic response.
boundary_notes: Failure regimes do not imply that the objective has no minimizer.
Transient safeguard activation is excluded unless it satisfies the chosen persistence rule.

notation.meaning: Set of failure classes active on \(K\).

source_refs.locator: Section 6.1, Algorithm 6.1.1 and equations (6.1.2)–(6.1.5), pp. 115–118; Sections 17.4.1–17.4.4, pp. 825–831

children.title: Model-Agreement Failure Regimes
children.top_down_role: Poor local fidelity, stale curvature, deficient sample geometry, and unreliable agreement diagnostics.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.statement_title: Model-agreement failure regime
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(A_k=f(x_k)-f(x_k+s_k)\), \(P_k=m_k(x_k)-m_k(x_k+s_k)>0\), and \(\rho_k=A_k/P_k\). Let \(N_k\geq0\) be a bound below which reduction comparisons are unresolved, and choose \(\tau_\rho>0\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: The regime concerns resolved discrepancies between objective and model. Noise-floor failures are excluded and classified separately.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A model-agreement failure regime is a persistent index set \(K\) such that, for every \(k\in K\), the reductions are resolved, \(\max\{|A_k|,|P_k|\}>N_k\), but the agreement error satisfies \(|\rho_k-1|>\tau_\rho\). It may be refined into poor local fidelity when the discrepancy remains large as \(\Delta_k\) is reduced; stale-curvature failure when the gradient-change residual \(\|\nabla f(x_k+s_k)-\nabla f(x_k)-H_ks_k\|\) exceeds a declared multiple of \(\|s_k\|\); deficient sample geometry when a derivative-free model fails its model-validity or poisedness test; and unreliable agreement computation when independently computed reductions disagree beyond their arithmetic error bounds. A regime is declared only after step feasibility and sufficient predicted reduction have been checked.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The regime consists of repeated, numerically resolved failures of the model to predict objective reduction. It can be refined by testing local fidelity under shrinking radii, the accuracy of the curvature prediction for gradient changes, derivative-free sample geometry, or the consistency of the reduction computation. An inadequate inner step or a ratio formed at the noise floor is excluded from this class.
assumptions_latex: \(P_k>0\) and the step satisfies the prescribed subproblem adequacy test.
The reductions exceed the declared numerical-resolution threshold.
Persistence is measured on a fixed diagnostic window or recurrent subsequence.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[K\subseteq\left\{k:\max\{|A_k|,|P_k|\}>N_k,\ \left|\frac{A_k}{P_k}-1\right|>\tau_\rho\right\}.\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: Since \(P_k>0\), the agreement error can be written \(|A_k-P_k|>\tau_\rho P_k\).
A one-sided rejection regime is obtained by replacing the symmetric test with \(\rho_k<\eta_1\).
special_cases_latex: For an exact quadratic objective with the exact quadratic model, \(A_k=P_k\) in exact arithmetic and the agreement-failure set is empty.
Near floating-point resolution, the ratio test is suspended rather than used as evidence of model failure.
immediate_consequences_latex: Persistent resolved rejection after verified inner adequacy is evidence against the current model-validity scale.
The equivalent discrepancy test avoids interpreting \(\rho_k\) without reference to \(P_k\).
boundary_notes: A single low ratio is an unsuccessful iteration, not necessarily a failure regime.
The definition does not identify whether the model error arose from derivatives, interpolation geometry, or stale curvature without an additional residual.

notation.meaning: Curvature operator or matrix used by the model.

children.title: Local Model Fidelity Failures
children.top_down_role: Failures caused by models that poorly represent local objective behavior.

knowledge_statements.title: Local Model Fidelity Failures
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Asymptotic boundary at which fully linear local fidelity is lost.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For radii \(\Delta_k\downarrow0\), models \(m_k\) centered at \(x_k\) lose fully linear local fidelity if at least one normalized error is unbounded:
\[
\limsup_{k\to\infty}
\frac{\sup_{\|p\|\le\Delta_k}|f(x_k+p)-m_k(p)|}{\Delta_k^2}=\infty
\]
or
\[
\limsup_{k\to\infty}
\frac{\sup_{\|p\|\le\Delta_k}\|\nabla f(x_k+p)-\nabla m_k(p)\|}{\Delta_k}=\infty.
\]
Consequently no constants independent of \(k\) can establish the usual fully linear value and gradient bounds along that sequence. Shrinking the radius alone therefore does not restore the required model accuracy.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Local fidelity fails when normalized value or gradient errors become unbounded as the radius shrinks, preventing uniform fully linear constants.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) and every \(m_k\) are continuously differentiable on the corresponding trust-region ball.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: An infinite displayed limit superior excludes uniform fully linear model bounds along the sequence.

notation.meaning: Local model centered at the current iterate.

source_refs.locator: 1.2.4 A Trust Region Model p. 35

source_witnesses.locator: 1.2.4 A Trust Region Model p. 35

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The normalized-error formulation is mathematically plausible as a sequence-level failure boundary, but the cited trust-region-model section does not inspectably support this exact fully linear asymptotic characterization. A source specifically defining fully linear models and uniform constants is required.

children.title: Agreement Diagnostic Failures
children.top_down_role: Unreliable predicted-versus-realized reduction assessments.

knowledge_statements.title: Agreement Diagnostic Failures
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Instability of the actual-to-predicted reduction ratio near a vanishing denominator.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let the true actual and predicted reductions be \(A_k=f(x_k)-f(x_k+p_k)\) and \(P_k=m_k(0)-m_k(p_k)>0\). Suppose computed function values produce \(\widehat A_k=A_k+e_k\), so the reported ratio is \(\widehat\rho_k=\widehat A_k/P_k\). The agreement diagnostic is unreliable along any sequence for which
\[
P_k\downarrow0
\quad\text{and}\quad
\limsup_{k\to\infty}\frac{|e_k|}{P_k}>0.
\]
Indeed, the ratio error satisfies \(|\widehat\rho_k-A_k/P_k|=|e_k|/P_k\), which need not vanish. Acceptance or rejection based on a fixed ratio threshold can then be reversed by evaluation error even when the local model is otherwise adequate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The agreement ratio becomes unreliable when predicted decrease vanishes while function-evaluation error remains comparable to that decrease.
assumptions_latex: \(\widehat A_k=A_k+e_k\) models the total error in the computed actual reduction.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: If \(P_k\to0\) while \(\limsup |e_k|/P_k>0\), the computed agreement ratio is not asymptotically reliable.

notation.meaning: Error in the computed actual reduction.

source_refs.locator: 6.1 The Basic Trust-Region Algorithm p. 115

source_witnesses.locator: 6.1 The Basic Trust-Region Algorithm p. 115

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The ratio-error identity is internally correct, but the evaluation-error failure boundary and threshold-reversal interpretation extend beyond the cited basic trust-region algorithm. A source treating noisy or inexact function evaluations in agreement ratios is required.

children.title: Stale Curvature Failures
children.top_down_role: Model defects arising from obsolete or misleading curvature information.

knowledge_statements.title: Stale Curvature Failures
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure caused by curvature information that no longer represents the current objective.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For the quadratic model \(m_k(p)=f(x_k)+g_k^Tp+\tfrac12p^TB_kp\), let \(H_k=\nabla^2f(x_k)\) and let \(P_k=m_k(0)-m_k(p_k)>0\). Curvature is diagnostically stale along a subsequence if
\[
\frac{|p_k^T(H_k-B_k)p_k|}{2P_k}\not\longrightarrow0.
\]
When the second-order Taylor remainder is \(o(\|p_k\|^2)\), this normalized mismatch is a nonvanishing leading contribution to the actual-versus-predicted reduction discrepancy. Thus repeatedly retaining \(B_k\) despite movement of \(H_k\) can prevent agreement ratios from approaching one, even as \(p_k\to0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Curvature is stale when its quadratic mismatch with the current Hessian remains significant relative to predicted decrease, obstructing asymptotic model agreement.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) is twice continuously differentiable near the relevant iterates.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A nonvanishing normalized curvature mismatch prevents the curvature term from becoming negligible in the agreement diagnostic.

notation.meaning: Curvature matrix retained by the model.
Predicted reduction of the computed step.

source_refs.locator: 6.1 The Basic Trust-Region Algorithm p. 115

source_witnesses.locator: 6.1 The Basic Trust-Region Algorithm p. 115

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The Taylor remainder being \(o(\|p_k\|^2)\) does not ensure that it is negligible relative to \(P_k\) unless an additional relation such as \(\|p_k\|^2/P_k=O(1)\) is imposed. The cited section also does not inspectably support this particular stale-curvature normalization.

children.title: Deficient Sample Geometry
children.top_down_role: Derivative-free model failures caused by poorly poised interpolation or regression samples.

knowledge_statements.title: Deficient Sample Geometry
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Poisedness failure for interpolation-based trust-region models.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(\mathcal P=\operatorname{span}\{\phi_1,\ldots,\phi_q\}\) be a finite-dimensional polynomial space and let \(Y_k=\{y_1,
\ldots,y_q\}\subset B(x_k,\Delta_k)\). Form the interpolation matrix \(V_k\in\mathbb R^{q\times q}\) by \((V_k)_{ij}=\phi_j(y_i)\). The sample geometry is deficient if \(V_k\) is singular. More generally, after scaling the ball to unit radius, it is numerically deficient when
\[
\kappa_2(\widetilde V_k)>K_V,
\]
for a prescribed threshold \(K_V>1\). Singularity makes the interpolating model nonunique or nonexistent; excessive conditioning amplifies errors in sampled function values and model coefficients.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Sample geometry is deficient when its interpolation matrix is singular or excessively ill-conditioned after normalization to the unit trust region.
assumptions_latex: The normalized basis and point scaling defining \(\widetilde V_k\) are fixed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\det(V_k)=0\) certifies algebraic deficiency, while \(\kappa_2(\widetilde V_k)>K_V\) flags numerical deficiency.

children.title: Subproblem Solver Failures
children.top_down_role: Undetected negative curvature, hard-case instability, premature termination, and oversolving.

knowledge_statements.title: Subproblem Solver Failures
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Checkable failure modes for an approximate quadratic trust-region solve.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Consider minimizing \(q_k(p)=g_k^Tp+\tfrac12p^TB_kp\) over \(\|p\|\le\Delta_k\), with \(B_k=B_k^T\). A computed pair \((p_k,\lambda_k)\) exhibits solver failure if any of
\[
\|p_k\|>(1+\tau_\Delta)\Delta_k,
\quad \|(B_k+\lambda_k I)p_k+g_k\|>\tau_r,
\quad \lambda_k<0,
\quad \lambda_{\min}(B_k+\lambda_k I)<-\tau_c
\]
holds, or if its predicted decrease is below a prescribed fraction of Cauchy decrease. These tests expose infeasibility, premature termination, invalid multiplier or curvature conditions, and missed negative curvature. Oversolving is present when inner residual reduction continues after all outer-required tests pass without changing the acceptance decision.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A trust-region subproblem solve fails when feasibility, residual, multiplier, curvature, or sufficient-decrease tests fail; unnecessary refinement after all tests pass is oversolving.
assumptions_latex: \(B_k=B_k^T\), \(\Delta_k>0\), and \(\lambda_k\) is the computed boundary multiplier.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Any displayed violation or failure of the Cauchy-decrease test certifies inadequate subproblem solution under the stated tolerances.

notation.meaning: Quadratic part of the trust-region model.
Computed multiplier for the radius constraint.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.statement_title: Trust-region subproblem solver failure
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Consider the quadratic subproblem \(\min_{\|s\|\leq\Delta}q(s)=g^Ts+\tfrac12s^THs\), with \(H=H^T\), \(\Delta>0\), and returned step \(\widehat s\). Let \(Q_C>0\) be the required Cauchy decrease and let \(j\) count inner iterations.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: The definition covers deterministic quadratic trust-region subproblem solvers, including truncated iterative methods and hard-case handling.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A subproblem solver failure is any returned state satisfying at least one of: infeasibility, \(\|\widehat s\|>\kappa_{\mathrm{tr}}\Delta\); insufficient reduction, \(q(0)-q(\widehat s)<\kappa_C Q_C\); missed negative curvature, when a computed direction \(d\) has \(d^THd<0\) but the returned step neither reaches the boundary along a decreasing curvature direction nor satisfies the prescribed second-order decrease; unacceptable optimality residual, when a claimed approximate minimizer has no \(\lambda\geq0\) for which \(\|(H+\lambda I)\widehat s+g\|\leq\epsilon_{\mathrm{in}}\), \(H+\lambda I\succeq-\epsilon_{\mathrm{curv}}I\), and \(|\lambda(\|\widehat s\|-\Delta)|\leq\epsilon_{\mathrm{comp}}\); or hard-case instability, when the solver loses the necessary component in a leftmost-eigenspace direction. Oversolving is the distinct effort fault \(j>j_{\\max}\) after an acceptable reduction certificate was already available.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The solver fails if it returns a step outside the allowed ball, fails to achieve the required model decrease, ignores detected negative curvature, falsely claims approximate optimality without satisfying residual, curvature, and complementarity tolerances, or mishandles the hard case. Continuing inner iterations after a sufficient certificate and beyond a declared effort limit is classified separately as oversolving.
assumptions_latex: The solver declares whether it is returning an approximate minimizer, a boundary step, or a negative-curvature step.
All inner tolerances and the effort limit are fixed by the inner–outer policy.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\mathrm{fail}(\widehat s)=\mathrm{true}\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad F_{\mathrm{feas}}\lor F_{\mathrm{dec}}\lor F_{\mathrm{nc}}\lor F_{\mathrm{KKT}}\lor F_{\mathrm{hard}}\lor F_{\mathrm{effort}}.\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: Sufficient reduction may be stated as a fixed fraction of the exact model-minimizer reduction when the minimizer is available.
Approximate optimality can be monitored through the shifted-system residual together with primal feasibility, curvature, and complementarity.
special_cases_latex: For positive-definite \(H\) with an unconstrained Newton step inside the ball, the multiplier is \(\lambda=0\).
When \(g=0\) and \(H\) has negative curvature, returning \(s=0\) is a missed-negative-curvature failure.
immediate_consequences_latex: A step may be adequate for the outer method without being an accurate global subproblem minimizer.
Hard-case handling requires spectral information not contained in the gradient Krylov space alone.
boundary_notes: Oversolving is a computational-effort failure, not a violation of subproblem optimality.
The tolerances must account for finite precision; exact KKT equalities are not required of a numerical solver.

children.title: Region-Control Failures
children.top_down_role: Radius collapse, unstable oscillation, persistently overlarge regions, and unsuitable initialization.

knowledge_statements.title: Region-Control Failures
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sequence-level failure predicates for trust-region radius updates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(\Delta_k>0\) be the radius, \(\chi_k\ge0\) a criticality measure, and \(R_k>0\) a radius below which the current model satisfies its adequacy test. Region control fails along a subsequence if any of the following occurs:
\[
\Delta_k\to0\ \text{ while }\ \liminf\chi_k>0,
\qquad
\liminf\Delta_k<\limsup\Delta_k\ \text{ with repeated alternating acceptances and rejections},
\]
or
\[
\liminf\frac{\Delta_k}{R_k}>1\ \text{ while model-inadequacy rejections persist}.
\]
These predicates respectively describe radius collapse away from stationarity, unstable radius oscillation, and a persistently overlarge region. An initial radius is unsuitable when it immediately triggers one of these regimes before a reliable model is established.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Radius control fails through collapse away from stationarity, persistent acceptance-rejection oscillation, or remaining larger than the scale where the model is adequate.
assumptions_latex: \(\Delta_k>0\), \(R_k>0\), and \(\chi_k\ge0\) are defined for each inspected iteration.
Acceptance and model-adequacy decisions use fixed tolerances.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Occurrence of any displayed sequence predicate identifies a distinct region-control failure regime.

notation.meaning: Largest diagnosed radius supporting model adequacy.

In particular, unequal radius limit inferior and superior with alternating decisions can occur during ordinary adaptive control and does not by itself identify unstable failure; the unsuitable-initial-radius clause is also not a precise predicate.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.statement_title: Trust-region radius-control failure
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(\Delta_k>0\), \(s_k\), and \(\rho_k\) be the radius, trial step, and agreement ratio. Fix \(0<\eta_1\leq\eta_2<1\), \(0<\gamma_1\leq\gamma_2<1\), a maximum radius \(\Delta_{\max}\), and a criticality residual \(\chi_k\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: The definition diagnoses deterministic radius management relative to a declared update policy. Alternative valid policies must substitute their own admissible update sets.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the basic update policy, define \(U_k=[\Delta_k,\Delta_{\max}]\) if \(\rho_k\geq\eta_2\), \(U_k=[\gamma_2\Delta_k,\Delta_k]\) if \(\eta_1\leq\rho_k<\eta_2\), and \(U_k=[\gamma_1\Delta_k,\gamma_2\Delta_k]\) if \(\rho_k<\eta_1\). A region-control failure occurs when \(\Delta_{k+1}\notin U_k\), or when one of the following persistent pathologies holds: radius collapse, \(\Delta_k\to0\) while \(\chi_k\geq\epsilon_\chi>0\) and resolved, adequate-model trials recur; unstable oscillation, repeated large expansion-contraction cycles without commensurate changes in resolved agreement; persistent overlarge regions, unsuccessful steps satisfy \(\|s_k\|_k\ll\Delta_k\) while contraction remains based on \(\Delta_k\) rather than step length; or unsuitable initialization, the initial radius is below the evaluation-noise scale or so large that repeated resolved rejection occurs before the model-validity scale is reached.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A radius-control failure is first any violation of the declared update intervals. It also includes persistent collapse away from criticality, repeated expansion-contraction cycles unsupported by model-agreement changes, retaining a radius far larger than repeatedly rejected steps, and initialization below the noise-resolvable scale or far above the model-validity scale.
assumptions_latex: The agreement ratios used by the controller are numerically resolved.
The step solver satisfies its feasibility and sufficient-decrease requirements.
The controller's thresholds and update factors are fixed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[F_k^{\mathrm{update}}=[\Delta_{k+1}\notin U_k],\qquad F^{\mathrm{region}}=F^{\mathrm{update}}\lor F^{\mathrm{collapse}}\lor F^{\mathrm{oscillation}}\lor F^{\mathrm{overlarge}}\lor F^{\mathrm{initial}}.\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: A step-length-based contraction replaces the unsuccessful interval by \([\bar\gamma_1\|s_k\|_k,\bar\gamma_2\|s_k\|_k]\).
Radius collapse away from criticality may be detected over a finite window by \(\Delta_{k+j}/\Delta_k\leq\tau_\Delta\) while \(\min_{0\leq j\leq w}\chi_{k+j}\geq\epsilon_\chi\).
special_cases_latex: Internal doubling is not oscillatory failure when each enlargement retains adequate agreement and increasing step length.
A small radius near a resolved stationary point is not radius collapse away from criticality.
immediate_consequences_latex: Using the step length after rejection prevents repeated evaluations of the same unacceptable interior step.
Every update-policy violation can be detected without knowing the minimizer of \(f\).
boundary_notes: Contraction after a resolved poor ratio is normal behavior, not a failure.
Noise-contaminated ratios must be diagnosed before attributing radius behavior to the controller.

notation.meaning: Admissible set for the next radius.

children.title: Evaluation Reliability Failures
children.top_down_role: Failures caused by ill-conditioning, rounding, inconsistent derivative accuracy, or changes below the evaluation-noise floor.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.statement_title: Evaluation-reliability failure taxonomy
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Suppose the computed oracle values satisfy \(\widetilde f(x)=f(x)+e_f(x)\), \(\widetilde g(x)=\nabla f(x)+e_g(x)\), and possibly \(\widetilde H(x)=\nabla^2f(x)+E_H(x)\). Let \(\widehat A_k\) and \(\widehat P_k\) be computed actual and predicted reductions, with certified or estimated error bounds \(B^A_k\) and \(B^P_k\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: The taxonomy applies to deterministic bounded-error and floating-point evaluations. Probabilistic oracle failures require confidence-qualified analogues.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: An evaluation-reliability failure is assigned one or more of the following labels. A reduction-resolution failure holds when \(|\widehat A_k|\leq B^A_k\) or \(|\widehat P_k|\leq B^P_k\), so the sign or ratio is not reliable. A cancellation failure holds when reductions are formed by subtracting large nearly equal values and the direct error bound exceeds a prescribed fraction of the predicted reduction. A derivative-consistency failure holds when \(\|e_g(x_k)\|>\epsilon_g^{\mathrm{orc}}\) or \(\|E_H(x_k)\|>\epsilon_H^{\mathrm{orc}}\), or when their errors exceed the accuracy budget required by the current \(\Delta_k\). An ill-conditioning failure holds when the scaled condition estimate makes the propagated evaluation error exceed the acceptance margin. A below-noise-step failure holds when the predicted or actual change is no larger than the objective noise floor. The agreement ratio is declared reliable only if \(\widehat P_k-B^P_k>0\) and both reduction errors are small relative to the decision margins.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The taxonomy distinguishes unresolved reductions, cancellation in differencing, inaccurate or inconsistent derivatives, amplification by ill-conditioning, and steps whose changes lie below the oracle noise floor. The actual-to-predicted ratio is usable only when the predicted reduction remains positive after accounting for error and both reduction errors are smaller than the acceptance margins.
assumptions_latex: The evaluation-error bounds are available or conservatively estimated.
The oracle-accuracy budgets are stated in the same norms as the model tests.
Acceptance decisions are suspended or safeguarded when the reliability predicate fails.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\operatorname{reliable}(\widehat\rho_k)\Rightarrow \widehat P_k-B^P_k>0,\quad B^A_k\ll|\widehat A_k|,\quad B^P_k\ll|\widehat P_k|.\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: With a relative machine-precision model, a practical resolution scale is \(N_k=c\varepsilon_M\max\{1,|f(x_k)|\}\).
For a quadratic model, computing \(P_k=-g_k^Ts_k-\tfrac12s_k^TH_ks_k\) directly avoids subtracting two large model values.
special_cases_latex: If both reductions are at the machine-precision scale, a safeguarded implementation may treat the iteration as successful rather than repeatedly shrinking the radius.
For a noisy objective, the initial radius should be large enough that expected model reduction exceeds the noise floor.
immediate_consequences_latex: A numerically unreliable ratio cannot by itself certify model inadequacy.
Shrinking the radius below the noise-resolvable scale can worsen rather than improve the agreement diagnostic.
boundary_notes: Oracle bias and random sampling error are distinct mechanisms even when both appear as reduction uncertainty.
Accurate function values do not imply accurate derivatives, and conversely.

notation.meaning: Error bounds for computed actual and predicted reductions.

children.title: Numerical Stability Failures
children.top_down_role: Failures associated with ill-conditioning, cancellation, or finite-precision effects.

knowledge_statements.title: Numerical Stability Failures
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Loss of reliability in the computed trust-region acceptance decision under rounding and linear-algebra errors.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let the exact actual and predicted reductions be \(a_k=f(x_k)-f(x_k+s_k)\) and \(p_k=m_k(0)-m_k(s_k)>0\). Suppose the computed reductions satisfy \(\widehat a_k=a_k+e_k^a\), \(\widehat p_k=p_k+e_k^p>0\), \(|e_k^a|\leq\delta_k^a\), and \(|e_k^p|\leq\delta_k^p\). For an acceptance threshold \(\eta\geq0\), define the exact and computed decisions by \(a_k\geq\eta p_k\) and \(\widehat a_k\geq\eta\widehat p_k\), respectively. The sufficient separation condition \[|a_k-\eta p_k|>\delta_k^a+\eta\delta_k^p\] guarantees that these decisions agree. If this condition fails, the error bounds alone do not certify agreement; when the inequality is strict in the opposite direction, admissible perturbations can move the computed margin across the threshold.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The exact and computed acceptance decisions are guaranteed to agree when the exact acceptance margin exceeds the combined error bound. At or below that bound, the error information alone cannot certify the decision, and admissible errors can place the computed margin at or across the threshold.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The regime \(|a_k-\eta p_k|\leq\delta_k^a+\eta\delta_k^p\) is a numerical-stability boundary at which agreement of the exact and computed acceptance classifications is not guaranteed by the error bounds.

notation.meaning: nonnegative bounds on the reduction errors

children.title: Scaling Failures
children.top_down_role: Failures caused by incompatible variable, objective, derivative, or radius scales.

knowledge_statements.title: Scaling Failures
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of trust-region geometry and step selection to remain covariant under a change of variable scales.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(x=Sz\), where \(S\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}\) is nonsingular and diagonal, so \(s_x=Ss_z\). The Euclidean trust region \(\|s_x\|_2\leq\Delta_x\) is represented in the \(z\)-coordinates by \(\|Ss_z\|_2\leq\Delta_x\). This set equals an isotropic ball \(\|s_z\|_2\leq\Delta_z\) if and only if \[S^TS=\left(\frac{\Delta_x}{\Delta_z}\right)^2I.\] In particular, equality with the same numerical radius requires \(S^TS=I\), whereas a uniform scaling permits equality after the corresponding radius adjustment. Thus, using identical unscaled Euclidean trust-region rules under a nonuniform rescaling generally changes the feasible steps and can change the algorithmic trajectory. With a scaled region \(\|D_xs_x\|_2\leq\Delta_x\), coordinate covariance is obtained by choosing a transformed metric satisfying \[D_z^TD_z=S^TD_x^TD_xS.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A Euclidean trust region becomes an ellipsoid under a nonuniform change of variable scales. It can be represented by another Euclidean ball only for a uniform scaling with a corresponding radius adjustment; otherwise the metric must be transformed to preserve the feasible steps.
assumptions_latex: \(S\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}\) is nonsingular and diagonal.
\(\Delta_x>0\) and, when an isotropic ball in the transformed coordinates is considered, \(\Delta_z>0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Nonuniform diagonal rescaling does not preserve an unscaled Euclidean trust-region ball; covariance requires the transformed metric \(D_z^TD_z=S^TD_x^TD_xS\).

trust-region radii in the two coordinate systems

children.title: Oracle Consistency Failures
children.top_down_role: Failures arising from inconsistent function, derivative, or model accuracy.

knowledge_statements.title: Oracle Consistency Failures
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Breakdown of first-order model adequacy when value and derivative oracles do not describe the same local function.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let a value oracle return \(F(x)\) and a gradient oracle return \(G(x)\), and form \(m_x(s)=F(x)+G(x)^Ts\). First-order consistency at \(x\) requires \[F(x+s)-F(x)-G(x)^Ts=o(\|s\|)\quad\text{as }s\to0.\] If instead there are \(c>0\) and steps \(s_j\to0\) such that \[|F(x+s_j)-F(x)-G(x)^Ts_j|\geq c\|s_j\|,\] then the model error is not of first-order Taylor size. Shrinking the trust-region radius along these steps cannot recover first-order agreement, so acceptance-ratio evidence cannot reliably validate the supplied gradient model.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If value and gradient oracles disagree to first order, shrinking the trust region cannot restore Taylor agreement or reliably validate the resulting model.
assumptions_latex: \(F:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\) and \(G:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^n\) are defined near \(x\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A residual of order \(\Omega(\|s\|)\) along vanishing steps is an oracle-consistency failure and prevents first-order local model adequacy.

notation.meaning: linear local model formed from the two oracles

children.title: Evaluation-Noise Floor Failures
children.top_down_role: Regimes where predicted or realized changes fall below reliable evaluation resolution.

knowledge_statements.title: Evaluation-Noise Floor Failures
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Acceptance-ratio resolution limit caused by bounded absolute noise in objective evaluations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose objective evaluations satisfy \(\widehat f(x)=f(x)+e(x)\) with \(|e(x)|\leq\varepsilon_f\). For a trial step, let \(a_k=f(x_k)-f(x_k+s_k)\), \(\widehat a_k=\widehat f(x_k)-\widehat f(x_k+s_k)\), and let the predicted reduction satisfy \(p_k>0\). Then \[|\widehat a_k-a_k|\leq2\varepsilon_f,\qquad |\widehat\rho_k-\rho_k|\leq\frac{2\varepsilon_f}{p_k},\] where \(\rho_k=a_k/p_k\) and \(\widehat\rho_k=\widehat a_k/p_k\). Thus, when \(p_k\) is comparable to or below \(2\varepsilon_f\), the ratio has order-one uncertainty and trust-region acceptance cannot be resolved from these evaluations alone.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Bounded evaluation noise causes order-one acceptance-ratio uncertainty once predicted reduction reaches the noise scale, so further radius contraction cannot resolve model quality.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: If \(p_k\leq2\varepsilon_f/\tau\), then \(|\widehat\rho_k-\rho_k|\) may be as large as \(\tau\), defining an evaluation-noise floor for any prescribed ratio resolution \(\tau>0\).
